_about: generated by tools/build_data.py from synthesis/; edit the source, not this file. One term per line: search for the term or an alias, read that line. Voices: plain first; designer and engineer on request.

terms.plain: The one strong color used for main buttons and for things you pick.
terms.designer: One accent keeps a calm, focused feel and makes color mean "you can act here". Add a second accent only when it has a job, not for decoration.
terms.engineer: Roles like color.bg.accent.bold, color.text.accent and color.border.focus alias color.accent.* steps. Accent text passes 4.5:1 and accent boundaries 3:1 in every mode.

terms.plain: A name that points to another choice instead of holding a value of its own.
terms.designer: A token that borrows another token's value, so one change flows down the chain. It is how semantic and component tokens stay linked to the palette.
terms.engineer: DTCG 2025.10: $value "{color.accent.light.9}" targets a whole token; {"$ref": JSON Pointer} reaches inside values. Chains are allowed; circular references are errors. Figma variables alias within one type.

terms.plain: The small pieces a part is built from, like the box, the words and the icon of a button.
terms.designer: The numbered parts of a component (container, label, icon) shown in its spec, so designers and engineers use the same names when discussing spacing, color and states.
terms.engineer: Named parts map to Figma layers or slots and to code sub-elements; planned component tokens name them: button.primary.container.color (proposed). EightShapes generates anatomy diagrams from layers.

terms.plain: A question that asks if you have something a person must make, like a logo.
terms.designer: For logo, app icon, icons, illustration, photography, brand type, motion, sound and more, OpenDesigner asks "Do you have this?", lists accepted formats and offers fallbacks; placeholders are always labeled.
terms.engineer: 19 rows in data/hooks.json (14 asset, 5 tool); asset rows carry ask, accepts, does and if_no. Statuses: have, commissioning, tool, open-library, placeholder, not-needed.
terms.designer_says: asset request: do you have this?

terms.plain: A screen width where the page changes its layout, like going to one column on a phone.
terms.designer: Each one is a moment the layout visibly reorganizes: panes appear, navigation moves from bar to rail. Fewer breakpoints mean bigger shifts; design mobile first.
terms.engineer: Material 600/840/1200/1600dp width breakpoints (Tailwind's set for web-only), written as rem media queries. DTCG has no breakpoint type, and OpenDesigner does not generate breakpoints yet.

terms.plain: A row of shades of one color, from very light to very dark.
terms.designer: Evenly stepped shades of one hue, usually 11 or 12 steps, so backgrounds, borders, hovers and text come from a set, not by eye.
terms.engineer: Ordered primitives like color.accent.light.1 to .12 plus a dark ramp: 12 steps generated in OKLCH as DTCG color objects with hex fallback; semantic tokens alias into them.
terms.example: Light blue for backgrounds, dark blue for text on them.

terms.plain: A ready piece of the screen, like a button, that you can use again and again.
terms.designer: A reusable part with defined anatomy, variants, sizes and states, styled only by tokens. OpenDesigner's catalog lists 64 canonical components in 10 categories, from Button to App shell.
terms.engineer: A Figma component with properties (variant, boolean, instance swap, text, slot) mirrored by a code component with props; Code Connect links them. Docs in opendesigner/components/<name>.md are planned.

terms.plain: A saved value for one part only, like the color of the main button.
terms.designer: Lets one component be restyled on its own (button.primary.bg) without changing every accent in the product. Add them only when a brand must tune that component separately.
terms.engineer: Planned tier 3, not generated yet: button.primary.bg (proposed) = "{color.bg.action.primary}" in component.tokens.json, only for components restyled independently or values shared by three or more.

terms.plain: A score for how much text stands out from what is behind it; higher is easier to read.
terms.designer: WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text, icons and control borders, 7:1 in high-contrast themes. Test colors as pairs, never alone.
terms.engineer: engine.py validate checks every foreground and background pair in every mode with no rounding (4.499:1 fails); APCA Lc 75 on body text is reported as an advisory note.
terms.example: 4.5:1 passes; 4.499:1 fails, because nothing is rounded.

terms.plain: How round the corners of a box or button are, from sharp to fully round.
terms.designer: The most varied visible lever across systems, from 0px to pill (median 6px). Radius should grow with component size, and nested corners stay concentric.
terms.engineer: CSS border-radius from tokens radius.0 to radius.32 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32) plus radius.full; the Roundness dial picks radius.control.

terms.plain: A dark version of the app where each color is picked with care, not flipped.
terms.designer: Map by role, not by value: each semantic color gets the dark step that keeps its light-mode contrast. Raised surfaces get lighter; accents soften to reduce glare.
terms.engineer: A resolver context (theme: dark) loading semantic.color.dark.tokens.json: same token names, re-pointed to other ramp steps (Atlassian 700 becomes 400). CSS scope via [data-theme] or prefers-color-scheme.

terms.plain: How tightly things are packed on the screen, from roomy to tight.
terms.designer: Dense layouts feel serious and focused and suit tables and dashboards; spacious ones feel calm and open. Density shrinks padding and row heights, never tap targets.
terms.engineer: A semantic-tier mode axis (semantic.density.compact|comfortable|spacious.tokens.json), separate from breakpoints and color; each step about 4px (Material -1 to -3). size.target.min stays fixed.

terms.plain: A file in your project that writes down each design choice for people and AI to read.
terms.designer: The living, readable record of the system. Each section states the decision and its reason, a token table, use and avoid notes and its zoom level.
terms.engineer: Generated at the project root by engine.py design-md from state.json, tokens and decisions.md, in Google's DESIGN.md format plus nine OpenDesigner sections; never edited as a source.

terms.plain: The shared rules and parts that make all the screens of an app look and work the same.
terms.designer: Foundations, tokens, components, patterns and the guidance and governance around them, so every team ships consistent, accessible screens without re-deciding color, type and spacing each time.
terms.engineer: OpenDesigner: opendesigner/state.json plus generated DTCG 2025.10 tokens, exports and DESIGN.md; component docs and lint rules are planned. Layers: context, principles, foundations, tokens, components, patterns, guardrails, delivery, governance.

terms.plain: Turning design choices into code that makes the real app look that way.
terms.designer: The step where decisions become tokens, CSS and components. When code is generated from the same source, what ships matches the design instead of being re-measured from mockups.
terms.engineer: engine.py export --format css|tailwind|swift|compose|dtcg writes opendesigner/build/. Tokens carry code syntax so Figma binds to variables; Code Connect makes Figma's MCP emit your components.

terms.plain: A color, size or other choice with a name, kept in one place for the whole app.
terms.designer: A named decision (brand blue, 16px spacing, 200ms fade) that design files and code both reference, so changing it once restyles every screen and nothing drifts.
terms.engineer: A DTCG 2025.10 object with a required $value and a $type such as color, dimension or duration, named by dot path (color.bg.accent) and compiled to CSS custom properties.
terms.example: Atlassian's space.100 token equals 8px.

terms.plain: A part that needs a real person to make it well, like a logo or photos.
terms.designer: Only 9 blocks, but the ones people notice first: brand marks, photography, illustration, motifs, custom icons, pictograms, sound, voice and tone. They are supplied or commissioned, never generated as final.
terms.engineer: Class D, provenance designer-owned in ontology.json (9 of 211 blocks). Its assets open hooks in data/hooks.json (H-logo to H-brandbook), each with formats, fallbacks and a briefed placeholder.

terms.plain: A shared way to write design choices that both design apps and code can read.
terms.designer: The open token format Figma, Penpot, Tokens Studio, Style Dictionary and Terrazzo support, so tokens move between tools without retyping. Stable since 28 Oct 2025.
terms.engineer: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10 plus Color and Resolver modules (a Final Community Group Report). Files are .tokens.json with $value, $type, $description, $extensions; themes go in .resolver.json.

terms.plain: How a move speeds up and slows down, like a car that pulls away and then brakes.
terms.designer: Decelerate curves make entrances feel quick and arriving; accelerate curves get exits out of the way; linear is only for spinners and progress. Keep a small named set.
terms.engineer: DTCG cubicBezier: four numbers, x values in [0, 1] and y unbounded, so overshoot is allowed; CSS cubic-bezier(). Defaults: standard (0.2, 0, 0, 1), exit (0.3, 0, 1, 1).

terms.plain: How high a part of the screen seems to float above the part below it.
terms.designer: Shows stacking order: most products visibly use three levels (resting, raised, overlay). Depending on the depth model it shows as shadow, lighter tone, border or glass.
terms.engineer: Semantic elevation.raised, .floating and .overlay: DTCG shadow arrays colored {color.shadow.key} and {color.shadow.ambient}, set by the depth model; in dark mode raised surfaces also step lighter.

terms.plain: A part that can be read from something you already have, like your logo or site.
terms.designer: Blocks best taken from what exists: your brand book, live product, repo or Figma file. Each value shows where it came from; you accept, adjust or ignore it.
terms.engineer: Class E, provenance extractable in ontology.json (2 of 211 blocks; many more can be pre-filled). Read at intake; each value carries its reference id, method and confidence.

terms.plain: Named colors and sizes kept in Figma, a design app, that can switch to dark mode.
terms.designer: Figma's version of tokens: color, number, string, boolean, timing and easing values in collections with modes, aliasable across collections and scoped to the right property pickers.
terms.engineer: Modes: 10 per collection on Professional, 20 on Organization. Native DTCG import takes one file per mode (sRGB/HSL colors, px, seconds); composites like typography do not import.

terms.plain: Big buttons that are close by are faster to hit than small ones far away.
terms.designer: Size targets generously and put the primary action near the content it acts on. Label key actions with text and icon. Screen-edge targets help mouse users but hurt touch users.
terms.engineer: T = a + b·log2(2D/w) (Fitts 1954). Encoded as size.target.min, fixed across densities, plus a lint error for targets under 24x24 CSS px.

terms.plain: The outline that shows which button or box you are on when you use the keyboard.
terms.designer: Must show on every background: a 2px ring, 2px offset, following the control's corner, in a color with 3:1 contrast. Never remove it.
terms.engineer: CSS outline on :focus-visible from focus.ring.width, focus.ring.offset and color.border.focus (per mode); radius.focus = radius.control + offset; forced-colors uses Highlight. WCAG 2.4.7 AA.

terms.plain: How thick or thin the letters are, from very thin to very bold.
terms.designer: Most systems use two to four weights: 400 body, 500-600 labels, 600-700 headings. Light (300) only at 32px and up. Weight-led hierarchy looks punchy; size-led looks airy.
terms.engineer: DTCG fontWeight: a number 1-1000 or an alias (thin 100 to black 900, extra-black 950); CSS font-weight. Expression sets type.weightCount 2-4; Energy sets heading weight 600-750.

terms.plain: The empty space between things lined up in a row, a column or a grid.
terms.designer: Even spacing between siblings set once on the container, so every list, toolbar and form keeps the same rhythm without per-item margins.
terms.engineer: CSS gap on flex and grid containers, from semantic dimension tokens like space.inline.sm = "{space.8}" or space.stack.lg. Figma: number variables scoped to gap.

terms.plain: A part the tool can work out by itself from a few of your answers.
terms.designer: About three quarters of a system, such as spacing, ramps, most tokens and components, follows from a few inputs and the eight dials. These get sensible defaults you adjust visually.
terms.engineer: Class G, provenance generatable in ontology.json (156 of 211 blocks): computed by the synthesis/levers.json formulas from raw inputs and dials, or a sourced default. Shown for adjustment.

terms.plain: We see things that sit close together, or inside the same box, as one group.
terms.designer: The best-evidenced visual principle, with a strength order: a shared boundary beats proximity, and proximity beats similarity. Keep space within groups clearly smaller than space between them.
terms.engineer: Enforced by construction: inner spacing tokens resolve below outer ones (innerOuterRatio 2 to 3.5 by density, in the space group's $extensions.opendesigner). Planned critique: flag containers nested over two deep.

terms.plain: Columns you can't see that help line things up across a page.
terms.designer: Columns, gutters and margins that align content. 4, 8 and 12 columns suit most products; 16 suits editorial or wide dashboards. Type never hangs into the gutter; containers may.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: grid.columns (proposed) as a number, grid.gutter and grid.margin (proposed) as dimensions per breakpoint, driving CSS grid-template-columns: 4, 8, 12 columns; 16-24px gutters.

terms.plain: The more choices you see, the longer it takes to pick, unless they are in groups or you can search.
terms.designer: Holds when choices are known and equally likely; newcomers scan lists one by one. Group, label, order and add search, and default one option. Never cut items to satisfy it.
terms.engineer: RT = a + b·log2(n) (Hick and Hyman 1952). Planned lint: warn on flat, ungrouped lists above roughly 10-12 items with no search, sections or typeahead (threshold inferred).

terms.plain: A small picture that stands for an action or thing, like a trash can for delete.
terms.designer: One library, stroke matched to body text weight, corners matched to Roundness. Label key actions; a meaningful icon standing alone needs a text alternative and 3:1 contrast.
terms.engineer: SVG on the library grid; size.icon.sm/md/lg = 16/20/24px; icon.stroke.sm/md/lg = 1.5/2/2.5px, scaled by size and label weight.

terms.plain: How close together or far apart the letters in a word sit.
terms.designer: Zero at body sizes, slightly positive (+0.02-0.05em) for small text and all caps, slightly negative from about 32px so big headlines feel dense and designed.
terms.engineer: DTCG letterSpacing is a dimension (px or rem only) inside typography, though em is the natural unit; CSS letter-spacing. Figma letter-spacing variables are px, not %.

terms.plain: How much room each line of text gets from top to bottom, so lines don't crowd.
terms.designer: Tight (1.1-1.25) makes headings solid; about 1.5 keeps paragraphs easy to follow. Bigger text wants a smaller ratio, longer lines a larger one; snap to 4px.
terms.engineer: Unitless number in the DTCG typography composite (lineHeight, a multiplier of fontSize); CSS line-height. Default: ratio rounded to the nearest 4px; Carbon ships compact 14/18 beside 14/20.

terms.plain: A check that runs by itself and flags a mistake, like too many text sizes.
terms.designer: Accessibility breaks are errors to fix before export; taste rules, such as more than 10 type sizes or bounce above 0.2, are warnings you may waive with a reason.
terms.engineer: engine.py validate runs deterministic checks and exits 1 on errors; findings cite their rule; waivers sit in state.json. A stylelint config in opendesigner/lint/ is planned (spec 7.12).

terms.plain: The empty space outside a box that keeps it away from the things next to it.
terms.designer: Space around an element or page edge. Prefer padding on the parent and gap between siblings; keep margins for page edges and layout sections so spacing stays predictable.
terms.engineer: CSS margin. Components set no outer margin; space.section.* spaces groups. Material's page margin is 16 compact, 24 above; page-margin tokens like layout.margin.compact (proposed) are not generated.

terms.plain: A common plug that lets an AI helper use other apps, like Figma.
terms.designer: Lets your AI assistant read and write in the tools you use: pull a Figma frame, push tokens to Figma variables or Paper, or show a visual picker inside chat.
terms.engineer: Model Context Protocol (spec 2026-07-28): servers expose tools, resources and prompts over stdio or remote HTTP; the MCP Apps extension renders server HTML in a sandboxed iframe.

terms.plain: One full set of the saved values, such as the light set or the dark set.
terms.designer: Swaps every value at once while names stay fixed: light or dark, compact or comfortable, standard or reduced motion. Designs switch mode instead of being redrawn.
terms.engineer: DTCG keeps modes in the resolver: a context (theme: light or dark) picks one file per mode, such as semantic.color.dark.tokens.json. Figma: a column per mode.

terms.plain: How long a move on screen lasts, most of the time well under a second.
terms.designer: Most UI motion runs 100-300ms: short feels snappy, long feels smooth, past about 500ms it drags. Make exits 20-35% shorter than entrances.
terms.engineer: DTCG duration tokens. At Energy 50: motion.duration.instant 0, micro 100, short 150, medium 250, long 400, extra 700ms; Energy scales medium and longer by 0.8-1.2.

terms.plain: Making an app look at home on your phone by using the phone's own buttons and letters.
terms.designer: System fonts and components almost everywhere, brand only in accents, content and voice. Feels at home and inherits OS updates like Liquid Glass, but looks more like other apps.
terms.engineer: At the low end, Brand presence 0-25 suggests the system font per platform and nativeShare near 1.0; below 50, a native lead platform keeps its own body size.

terms.plain: The grays for text, backgrounds and lines, at times with a faint hint of color.
terms.designer: Pure gray reads neutral and tool-like, suiting photo and data apps; a slight tint toward the brand, warm or cool sets the product's temperature.
terms.engineer: A 12-step ramp per theme: color.neutral.light.1 to .12 and color.neutral.dark.*. Tinted ramps keep OKLCH chroma about 0.01-0.03 mid-ramp, 0-0.008 at the ends.

terms.plain: A way to write a color by how light it is, how strong it is and which color it is.
terms.designer: A perceptual color space: blue 600 and green 600 look equally heavy, so ramps stay balanced and hue swaps keep hierarchy. HSL makes yellows wash out and blues go muddy.
terms.engineer: CSS oklch(L C H), Baseline since May 2023; Tailwind v4 uses it for its whole palette. DTCG color object: colorSpace "oklch", components [L, C, H], optional hex fallback.

terms.plain: A choice only your team can make, like who the app is for or which devices it runs on.
terms.designer: Business decisions, not design work: scope, audience, platforms, principles, governance, terminology. OpenDesigner asks them, pre-fills from hints in your repo or references, and never invents an answer.
terms.engineer: Class I, provenance owner-input in ontology.json (21 of 211 blocks), so business decisions are not misfiled as designer-owned. Class I questions are asked or pre-filled, never invented.

terms.plain: The empty space inside a box, between its edge and what is in it.
terms.designer: Inner breathing room of buttons, cards and fields. Keep it smaller than the space between groups so related things read together; parents own spacing, children never add outer margins.
terms.engineer: CSS padding, fed by semantic inset tokens such as space.inset.md = "{space.12}" (dimension). Density modes shrink insets one scale step; Material uses padding and gap before margins.

terms.plain: A tried way to put parts together for a common job, like a sign-up form.
terms.designer: A composition of components plus behavior rules for a recurring task: forms, validation, search and filtering, empty states, onboarding. It encodes when to use it, not only how it looks.
terms.engineer: 13 patterns (L08 P1 to P13), each listing the catalog components it composes, its key decisions and evidence-backed rules; stored under the pat.* ontology layer.
terms.designer_says: UX pattern for a recurring task

terms.plain: The way a phone or computer expects things like menus and going back to work.
terms.designer: Share what users perceive as the brand (color, type personality, illustration, voice); adopt the platform's version of how the device works: navigation, back, sheets, pickers, text fields, system icons.
terms.engineer: The behavior.navigationNative param is true at every Brand presence value. Mapping tokens to platform colors, such as color.text.primary to iOS label, is planned; exports emit literal values.

terms.plain: A raw value with a plain name, like "blue 500", that says what it is, not what it is for.
terms.designer: The raw palette and scales (blue.500, space.200) with no meaning attached. Designers pick from semantic tokens instead; primitives are the ingredients those tokens point to.
terms.engineer: Bottom tier: single-valued tokens such as color.accent.light.9 (OKLCH color object) or space.16 (dimension). Values never change per mode; semantic tokens alias them. File: primitives.tokens.json.
terms.example: blue.500 is a primitive; it knows its color but not its job.

terms.plain: Showing only what you need now and keeping the rest out of sight until you ask.
terms.designer: Main options up front, advanced ones behind a clearly labeled trigger such as "More options" or an accordion. Keep it to two levels, and never hide essentials behind hover.
terms.engineer: Ontology node pat.disclosure; no DTCG type, it composes components. Built from C53 Accordion or disclosure using the WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern, at most two levels deep.

terms.plain: A setting on your phone or computer that asks apps to move less, for people who get dizzy.
terms.designer: Treat WCAG 2.3.3 as required, though it is AAA. Keep feedback (color and opacity changes, crossfades); remove travel: sliding, scaling, parallax and bounce.
terms.engineer: Web @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce); iOS Reduce Motion, Android Remove animations. OpenDesigner's motion mode (motion.reduced.tokens.json): short fades, movement at 0ms, no translate or scale.
terms.example: With Reduce Motion on, a sliding panel fades in place.

terms.plain: Looking at a site you like to learn how it is built, without copying its name or logo.
terms.designer: Carries structure and quality, never identity: no name, logo, photos, copy or proprietary fonts. A reference's brand color lends its role and strength, not its hex.
terms.engineer: The opendesigner-extract skill reads a URL, screenshot, Figma file, repo CSS or brand book; engine.py intake runs the LEVERS formulas backwards to proposed dials, accepted with --set-by reference --source-ref.

terms.plain: A small file that says which value files to mix for each look, like light or dark.
terms.designer: The recipe behind themes: it lists the token sets and switches (theme, brand, density) and which one wins, so tools produce every light, dark or brand combination consistently.
terms.engineer: DTCG Resolver Module 2025.10: version, sets, modifiers with contexts, and resolutionOrder (later entries win). OpenDesigner writes opendesigner.resolver.json; Terrazzo supports resolvers, Style Dictionary v5 does not.

terms.plain: A value named for its job, like "page background", that points to a raw value below it.
terms.designer: Named by role, not by look: color.bg.accent, color.text.subtle. Themes, dark mode and rebrands re-point these names, so designs stay correct without touching every screen.
terms.engineer: Tier 2: $value is a reference, color.bg.accent.bold = "{color.accent.light.9}". Modes live here; each resolver context re-points it (dark: {color.accent.dark.9}).
terms.example: Page background is white in light mode and near-black in dark.

terms.plain: A soft dark patch drawn under something to make it look lifted off the page.
terms.designer: Two layers read realistic: a sharp contact shadow for the edge and a soft blur for distance, tinted neutral rather than pure black. Shadows are decorative, so boundaries need contrast.
terms.engineer: DTCG shadow: an object or array of {color, offsetX, offsetY, blur, spread, inset}, emitted as CSS box-shadow. Alias color to {color.shadow.key} so dark mode can swap it.

terms.plain: The first quick pass: a whole but rough design system from a few answers.
terms.designer: A handful of questions (scope, audience, platforms, brand, color, logo) yield a complete but coarse system you can use right away, then refine area by area.
terms.engineer: Zoom level 0: the six zoom0 questions in pacing.json; every other decision keeps its auto_default, so the engine still generates a complete token set and DESIGN.md.
terms.designer_says: quick sketch of the whole system

terms.plain: A folder of instructions an AI helper reads so it knows how to do one job well.
terms.designer: A packaged way of working you load into your own AI tool. OpenDesigner ships as skills: install them and your assistant runs the design-system interview and writes the files.
terms.engineer: Agent Skills format: a folder with SKILL.md (name and description frontmatter) and optional scripts/, references/ and assets/. Loaded by Claude, ChatGPT and Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and more.

terms.plain: The one place where you change a value; every other copy is made from it.
terms.designer: Decide where edits happen first. Whichever side is not the source drifts unless sync is automatic, so Figma becomes a synced view, not a second master.
terms.engineer: In OpenDesigner, opendesigner/state.json plus the DTCG tokens it generates; DESIGN.md, CSS, Swift, Compose, Figma and Paper are generated views. Code-canonical remains an option for mature systems.

terms.plain: A short list of gap sizes the whole app picks from, like marks on a ruler.
terms.designer: A 4px grid with an 8px rhythm, about 15 steps from 0 to 96. Steps differ enough that tight-within, loose-between grouping reads at a glance.
terms.engineer: Dimension primitives space.0 to space.96 in px, named by value (space.16 = 16px); components use semantic aliases like space.inset.md = "{space.12}", never raw steps.

terms.plain: Movement that acts like a real spring, coming to rest with maybe a small bounce.
terms.designer: Defined by stiffness and damping instead of a fixed time, so motion feels natural and keeps its speed when interrupted. Use bounce for spatial hero moments; fades stay critically damped.
terms.engineer: No DTCG spring type: store dampingRatio and stiffness (M3 standard 0.9 and 700) in $extensions.opendesigner, derive duration and bounce for Apple, and sample into CSS linear() for web.

terms.plain: How a part looks at a moment, like when you point at it, press it, or it is off.
terms.designer: Style enabled, hover, focus-visible, pressed, selected, disabled, loading and error. States that carry meaning need 3:1 against neighbors; touch screens have no hover, so never hide essentials there.
terms.engineer: CSS :hover, :focus-visible, :active, :disabled plus aria-*. Hover and press shift one and two ramp steps (color.bg.accent.bold-hover, bold-pressed); opacity.state.hover covers unknown colors.

terms.plain: Colors that tell you how things went, like green for good and red for a problem.
terms.designer: Success, warning, error and info, each with subtle and bold levels. Never rely on color alone: pair with an icon and text, and put dark text on yellow fills.
terms.engineer: color.bg.<status>.subtle, .bold, .bold-hover; color.text.<status>, color.border.<status>; icons use color.text.<status>. Text 4.5:1, icons and borders 3:1. Color-only meaning: planned lint error.

terms.plain: A background layer that things sit on, like a card on a page.
terms.designer: Stacked background levels (sunken, base, raised, overlay) that separate page, cards and popovers. Light mode separates them with subtle tone plus shadow or border; dark mode with lighter tones.
terms.engineer: Role-named color tokens re-pointed per theme: color.surface.sunken, .base, .raised, .overlay, plus .nav and .tinted. Compare Material 3 surface-container-lowest to -highest and Carbon $layer-01 to 03.

terms.plain: A ready page plan made from bigger pieces, like a settings page.
terms.designer: A page-level arrangement of patterns and components that sets content structure before real content arrives. The catalog covers dashboard, list, detail, settings and marketing landing pages.
terms.engineer: Five templates in L08, each mapped to catalog ids: a dashboard uses C63 app shell, C33 sidebar, C52 cards and C57 table.
terms.code_name: L08 template mapped to catalog ids

terms.plain: A named look for the whole app, such as your brand in dark mode.
terms.designer: A named combination (Brand A, dark, high contrast) applied across the system. Keep brand, color scheme and density as separate axes so combinations need not be drawn by hand.
terms.engineer: One permutation of DTCG resolver modifiers; outputs multiply (4, 3 and 2 contexts give 24). Keep modifiers orthogonal. CSS export emits one [data-theme] scope per context.

terms.plain: A part a coder can make with a named tool, with a few things to watch for.
terms.designer: Blocks an engineer can produce with a named tool, with a caveat: font sourcing, icons, voice drafting and the token pipeline. OpenDesigner recommends the tool and states the catch.
terms.engineer: Class T, provenance tool-assisted in ontology.json (23 of 211 blocks): OpenDesigner names the tool (Terrazzo, Figma MCP, Code Connect), runs or links it, states the caveat, records the choice.
terms.code_name: class T, tool named and recorded

terms.plain: The area you can tap to press a button, which can be bigger than what you see.
terms.designer: Minimum hit area: 24 by 24 CSS px on web (WCAG 2.2 AA), 44pt on Apple, 48dp on Android. Visuals may shrink with density; hit areas never do.
terms.engineer: size.target.min, fixed across density modes: 24 CSS px web, 44pt iOS, 48dp Android. engine.py validate errors when a target token falls below its floor.

terms.plain: The short list of text sizes an app uses, from small labels to big titles.
terms.designer: Sizes grown from a base by a ratio: 1.125-1.2 feels calm and dense, 1.25 suits product plus marketing, 1.333+ feels editorial. Use three sizes or fewer per view.
terms.engineer: size(n) = base x ratio^n, rounded to whole pixels; stored as font.size.* dimension primitives. Expression sets type.ratio 1.2/1.25/1.333; Density above 66 caps it at 1.2.
terms.example: Base 16 at ratio 1.25 gives 16, 20, 25, 31, 39.

terms.plain: A set of letters that all share one look, like the letters on an iPhone.
terms.designer: The main personality choice in type: system fonts feel native, open faces like Inter feel neutral, proprietary faces like Plex or Cereal feel brand-led. Check licence and script coverage early.
terms.engineer: DTCG fontFamily: a string or an array in fallback order, e.g. ["Inter", "system-ui", "sans-serif"]. Emitted as CSS font-family; Figma import accepts a single string only.
terms.example: SF Pro on Apple devices, Roboto on Android.

terms.plain: Another look for the same part, like a bold main button and a plain second one.
terms.designer: Styled versions of one component that signal emphasis or purpose: primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive. Keep one primary per view; a lint warning for more is planned.
terms.engineer: A Figma variant property plus code prop (variant="primary"), styled by roles like color.bg.action.primary, not yet by button.primary.bg (proposed). Variants multiply with size and state.

terms.plain: The order your eye sees things on a screen, set by size, boldness, color and place.
terms.designer: Guide attention by importance: one dominant element, three distinct levels, no more than three type sizes and one primary action per view. If everything looks the same, nothing stands out.
terms.engineer: Levers: type.ratio from Expression and emphasis.maxPrimaryPerView = 1 (recorded, not checked yet); a warning above 3 type sizes per view is planned. Role tokens stay decoupled from HTML headings.

terms.plain: The main rule book that helps apps and sites work for people who can't see, hear or move well.
terms.designer: Version 2.2, level AA, is the usual target: text contrast 4.5:1, non-text contrast 3:1, visible focus, 24 by 24 CSS px minimum targets. AAA is stricter.
terms.engineer: Criteria OpenDesigner builds in: 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 contrast, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.5.8 target size (AA), and 2.3.3 animation from interactions (AAA).

terms.plain: How far one part of your design has come, from a rough sketch to full detail.
terms.designer: Everyone starts with a sketch of the whole system, then zooms into any area and can stop at any level with something that works. DESIGN.md shows each section's level.
terms.engineer: Levels 0 sketch, 1 broad, 2 defined, 3 detailed (references/pacing.json). Questions carry a zoom field; a stage asks only those at or below the level being worked.

terms.plain: Does every making step in one go, then checks the result for problems.
terms.designer: The one command to run at the end of a step or session. It rebuilds values, exports, guides and preview, then reports any problems.
terms.engineer: engine.py build runs generate and validate, then (no errors, or --force) design-md, export and preview, exporting only the chosen platforms' code files. Exits 1 on errors.
terms.example: Run build before you show the result to your team.

terms.plain: Writes two short, easy pages: one about how your app looks, and one about what it is for.
terms.designer: Produces the readable guide to the system and a separate product brief. Hand-written notes survive only inside keep blocks; the rest is rebuilt from decisions.
terms.engineer: engine.py design-md [--out DIR] renders DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md at the project root from state.json, tokens and decisions.md; only <!-- od:keep --> blocks survive regeneration.
terms.example: Run it after each choice so the guide stays current.

terms.plain: Copies your design into the forms that websites, phone apps and design tools can read.
terms.designer: Hands the system to each place it lives: web styles, a Tailwind theme, Figma variables, Paper, iOS and Android code, all from one source.
terms.engineer: engine.py export --format css|tailwind|figma|paper|swift|compose|dtcg|artifact|brand|all writes a folder per format in opendesigner/build/, like css/tokens.css or brand/index.html.
terms.example: Export to Tailwind for the website and Swift for the iPhone app.

terms.plain: Notes a problem or idea about this tool, so you can send it to the people who make it.
terms.designer: Captures gaps, bugs, confusing steps and ideas while you work, ready to send to the project as an issue. Nothing is posted unless you say yes.
terms.engineer: engine.py feedback "text" --kind gap|bug|confusing|idea (default idea) appends an F-nnn entry to opendesigner/feedback.md and prints a pre-filled GitHub issue link. Nothing is posted.
terms.example: A question you had to ask twice becomes a confusing note.

terms.plain: Turns your saved choices into the full list of colors, sizes and spacing your app will use.
terms.designer: Rebuilds every design value from your decisions, including light and dark, density and reduced motion. Run it after each step that changes values.
terms.engineer: Writes opendesigner/tokens/: DTCG 2025.10 files per tier and mode (primitives, semantic, semantic.color.light.tokens.json and .dark, density, motion), opendesigner.resolver.json and opendesigner.meta.json.
terms.example: Change the brand color, then generate to see new shades.

terms.plain: Starts a new, blank design in your project, with safe first answers already filled in.
terms.designer: The first step of a session. It opens a system on sourced defaults, so every later choice is a change from a known starting point.
terms.engineer: engine.py init [--name "Acme"] [--from path] [--force] creates ./opendesigner/state.json from levers.json defaults and opens decisions.md with entry D-0001. Refuses to overwrite without --force.
terms.example: Type init once, then answer the first question.

terms.plain: Looks at the sizes in a site or file you like and turns them into first ideas for your design.
terms.designer: Turns what was measured on a reference, like its corner radii or type sizes, into proposed dial positions. Nothing changes until you accept. Competitor references propose nothing.
terms.engineer: engine.py intake <measurements.json> [--accept] [--json] fits reference measurements to proposed dials and raw inputs with confidence levels; --accept records each as set --set-by reference --source-ref <ref-id>.
terms.example: A site with round buttons suggests a high roundness dial.

terms.plain: Lock keeps a choice safe so no one changes it by mistake, and unlock lets it change again.
terms.designer: Protects decisions that must not drift, such as brand colors or accessibility floors. Unlocking needs the owner's clear consent, so later sessions cannot quietly restyle them.
terms.engineer: engine.py lock <path>, engine.py unlock <path>. Sets locked on the answer or dial record, or adds the path to state.json locks; set refuses locked paths without --force.
terms.example: Lock the brand teal so no one swaps it later.

terms.plain: Saves your answer to one question in the chat, along with your reason.
terms.designer: The shortcut for answering an interview question by its id. One answer can also move linked dials, such as corner softness setting roundness.
terms.engineer: engine.py pick <Q-id> <option-value> --why "reason". Same as set on answers.<Q-id>; mapped answers also set dials or raw inputs (Q-shape-01 subtle sets dials.roundness to 40).
terms.example: Pick subtle corners for a busy work tool.

terms.plain: Makes one web page that shows every color, size and shape in your design, with a few sample parts.
terms.designer: Builds a single specimen page of every value and a few components, light and dark side by side, so you can judge the system by eye.
terms.engineer: engine.py preview [--open] writes opendesigner/preview.html, a self-contained specimen of every token and a few components in light and dark; --open launches it in the browser.
terms.example: Open the preview to see buttons and cards in both modes.

terms.plain: Shows the exact numbers your choices lead to, like a recipe card for the whole look.
terms.designer: Shows the real dial positions and every value they lead to, such as type ratio or control radius, so the options you are shown use real numbers.
terms.engineer: engine.py resolve prints JSON: effective dials (explicit, then preset, coupling and macros, clamped 0-100), dialSources, macroConflicts, zoom and every derived param. Read-only; fills template payloads.
terms.example: Roundness 45 resolves to a real corner size in pixels.

terms.plain: Saves one choice and the reason you gave, so it is never lost or forgotten.
terms.designer: Records a single decision with its rationale. Later sessions see what was chosen and why, instead of guessing from the finished look.
terms.engineer: engine.py set <path> <json-value> --why "reason" [--set-by delegated] [--lock]. Writes state.json and appends a D-nnnn entry to decisions.md; locked paths need unlock or --force.
terms.example: Set the brand color to teal because it matches the logo.

terms.plain: Checks your design for problems, like text too faint to read or buttons too small to tap.
terms.designer: Runs the checks a careful reviewer would: text contrast, target sizes, naming and unused values. Fix every error before showing results; warnings are worth a look.
terms.engineer: engine.py validate [--json] checks contrast pairs per theme, that every resolver permutation resolves, target floors, DTCG structure and lint. Exits 1 on errors, 0 with warnings; findings cite rules.
terms.example: Gray text on a gray card fails and must be fixed.

terms.plain: A button that copies your picks as short lines of text, ready to paste back into the chat.
terms.designer: Closes the loop between looking and deciding: your pick, an optional note and a lock box become text the model applies exactly, with no retyping.
terms.engineer: The #copy button in every template writes OD: lines to the clipboard (navigator.clipboard, execCommand fallback); the note field adds --why and the lock checkbox adds OD:lock lines.
terms.example: Pick soft corners, press the button, paste in chat.

terms.plain: A list in the design guide of what to do and what to avoid, for people and AI helpers.
terms.designer: The guide's rules in plain sentences: what the system guarantees, the do's (one primary action per view) and don'ts (never shrink hit areas), plus any waivers.
terms.engineer: Section 8 of DESIGN.md (## Do's and Don'ts), written by design-md: rules enforced by construction, Do and Don't bullets, current validation findings and waivers with reasons.
terms.example: Don't use motion as the only signal.

terms.plain: A short block of settings at the top of the design guide, set out so a computer can read it.
terms.designer: The machine-readable header of the design guide: main colors, type styles, corner radii, spacing and key components, so other AI tools pick up the look quickly.
terms.engineer: YAML front matter in DESIGN.md using only Google's DESIGN.md keys (version, name, description, colors, typography, rounded, spacing, components), filled from default-mode semantic tokens. DTCG files stay canonical.
terms.example: primary: the main brand color as a hex value.

terms.plain: A short note, added only if you say yes, that tells new AI helpers to read your design rules first.
terms.designer: Keeps later AI sessions on-system: they read the design guide and values before touching UI, stop hard-coding values, and ask before changing locked decisions.
terms.engineer: assets/output/AGENTS-snippet.md, appended to AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md after asking: read DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md and tokens first, never hard-code values, run engine.py review after implementation.
terms.example: A new AI session reads it before styling a page.

terms.plain: The folder with ready copies of your design for web pages, phone apps and design tools.
terms.designer: Where the exports land, one per tool the team uses: web styles, Tailwind theme, Figma import files, Paper, iOS and Android. Rebuilt, never edited by hand.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/build/: css and tailwind (web), swift (iOS), compose (Android), figma, paper, dtcg. build writes the chosen platforms' code files; export --format all writes every one.
terms.example: Your web app imports the file in css.

terms.plain: A diary of every choice made, with how it was made, when and why.
terms.designer: The running history of the system: each decision with its reason, how it was set and whether it is locked. Teammates read it to learn why.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/decisions.md is append-only, ADR-style. Each set, pick, lock and init adds a D-nnnn entry: path = value, set_by, locked, date, supersedes, source_ref and reason.
terms.example: D-0002: corners set to subtle because it is a dense tool.

terms.plain: A list of problems and ideas you found while using this tool, kept so you can send them in later.
terms.designer: A running list of gaps, bugs, confusing steps and ideas noticed during a session, kept on your machine until you choose to send them to the project.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/feedback.md, appended by engine.py feedback: one F-nnn entry per note with date, kind and a pre-filled issue link. Stays local; the person submits the issue.
terms.designer_says: running list of gaps and ideas
terms.example: F-001: no question about chart colors in dark mode.

terms.plain: A single web page that lets you see your whole design at once, in light and dark.
terms.designer: A specimen sheet for judging the system as a whole: colors, type, spacing, corners, depth and sample components, light and dark side by side.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/preview.html, written by engine.py preview or build: one self-contained HTML file that uses the generated CSS variables to show every token and a few components.
terms.example: Open it in any browser, with no setup.

terms.plain: A short page about your product: who it is for, what it does and where it runs.
terms.designer: The product brief kept apart from the visual system: audience, surfaces, the memorable thing, ranked principles, constraints and scope. It changes at a different pace than the look.
terms.engineer: PRODUCT.md at the project root, rendered by engine.py design-md from state.json context. Headings: Product, Audience, Surfaces, Memorable Thing, Principles, Constraints, Scope, Team and Governance.
terms.example: An invoicing app for small shop owners, on web and iPhone.

terms.plain: A one-page note that tells your team, in plain words, why the design looks the way it does.
terms.designer: A one-page case for teammates who will not read the log: the five choices that shape everything, what the rules guarantee, and what is still open.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/RATIONALE.md, written by the model (not the engine) from decisions.md using assets/output/RATIONALE.md; refreshed after each extend session; ids only in footnotes.
terms.example: We chose soft corners because the app is for families.

terms.plain: The one file that holds all your answers and settings; everything else is made from it.
terms.designer: The single record of every answer, dial position, brand input and asset status. Change the system by changing a decision here through the engine, never by editing outputs.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/state.json (schema opendesigner-state/1): answers {Q-id: {value, set_by, locked, decision}}, dials 0-100, raw inputs, overrides, hooks, locks, zoom, hashes. Tokens and views generate from it.
terms.example: Your brand color and corner choice both live here.

terms.plain: The folder that holds the main list of every color, size and timing in your design.
terms.designer: The source of truth for every design value. Figma, CSS and app code are copies made from it, so a change here reaches all of them.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/tokens/: canonical DTCG 2025.10 files, one per tier and mode (primitives.tokens.json, semantic.color.dark.tokens.json), plus opendesigner.resolver.json. Written by generate; never hand-edited.
terms.example: The dark mode colors sit in their own file here.

terms.plain: Shows where art like your logo stands: you have it, someone is making it, or it is not needed.
terms.designer: Tracks assets only a person should create, such as logo, icons or photos: have, commissioning a designer, open library, a named tool, placeholder, or not needed.
terms.engineer: hooks.<H-id>.status in state.json: pending (until asked), have, commissioning, tool, open-library, placeholder or not-needed. Set with engine.py set hooks.H-logo.status '"have"'; other values are rejected.
terms.example: Logo: commissioning, since a designer is drawing it.

terms.plain: A rule OpenDesigner follows in every project, taken from experts its makers trust. You can still ask to change it.
terms.designer: Craft rules from the sources the OpenDesigner owner marked non-negotiable. They are applied and locked from the start; your explicit override or your own project standard wins.
terms.engineer: Kept in synthesis/standards.json, versioned, shipped as references/standards.json. A project follows the ones whose applies_to tags match its platforms and stack.
terms.example: A house standard stops menus from growing out of nothing.

terms.plain: The step-by-step chat where the AI asks you one big question at a time and saves your answers.
terms.designer: A guided conversation that starts with a quick sketch of the whole system, then zooms into the areas you care about, one high-impact question per turn.
terms.engineer: Run by the opendesigner skill: questions from references/stages/, metadata in questions.json, pacing in pacing.json; each answer goes through engine.py pick or set into state.json.
terms.example: First question: what are you making?

terms.plain: A short line of text that stands for one choice, which you paste back into the chat.
terms.designer: The one format every click and reply turns into, so a choice made in a visual picker lands in the record exactly, with an optional reason and lock.
terms.engineer: A line starting OD: (set, lock, unlock, accept, ignore, remix), such as OD:set Q-shape-01="subtle" --why "dense tool", applied with engine.py set or lock.
terms.example: OD:set dials.roundness=65 means softer corners (12px).

terms.plain: A short name tag for each question, so you can go back and change that answer any time.
terms.designer: The stable handle for a question across sessions. Say "change Q-shape-01" and any later session finds the same decision, its history and what it affects.
terms.engineer: Format Q-<area>-<nn>, such as Q-shape-01, listed in questions.json. engine.py set turns a bare Q-id into answers.<Q-id>; decisions.md entries carry it.
terms.example: Q-color-01 is the question about your brand color.

terms.plain: The answer the AI suggests, with a reason, and it only counts once you say yes.
terms.designer: Every question comes with one suggested option and a short reason tied to your answers, with sources on request. Accepting it records a confirmed default, not your own choice.
terms.engineer: Listed first among 2 to 4 options on the question card, with its reason in brackets. Accepting records --set-by confirmed_default; a recommendation is never logged as chosen.
terms.example: Subtle corners, because your app is a busy work tool.

terms.plain: Writing each page so tools that answer questions pick it to quote.
terms.designer: Each page answers one real question in its first sentence, under a heading in the words people type.
terms.engineer: references/probe.md: a few questions by hand, logged out; record each engine's searches, sources and follow-ups. fixes.md turns them into page changes.
terms.example: Answer "how much does it cost?" in the first line of the pricing page.

terms.plain: Helping AI chat tools like ChatGPT read your site and name it in their answers.
terms.designer: Real facts, quotes and named sources make AI answers more likely to use a page; repeating keywords makes it less likely.
terms.engineer: Allow OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot in robots.txt; GPTBot and ClaudeBot only gather training data. search.py robots lists each bot.
terms.example: Let ChatGPT's search crawler in, even if training crawlers stay out.

terms.plain: Making your pages easy for search sites like Google to find, read and show.
terms.designer: How pages are named, titled, linked and described, so search results show them and people choose to click.
terms.engineer: search.py audit <build folder> checks robots.txt, sitemap.xml, canonicals, titles, descriptions, the h1 and JSON-LD in the served HTML. Read-only.
terms.example: Give the pricing page its own title so search shows it.
source: Google Search Central, AI features and your website (read 2026-11-07)

terms.plain: A rule your design always follows. It is set for you, and only you can ask to change it.
terms.designer: A non-negotiable rule from a source you or OpenDesigner trust, such as your brand book. It is applied without asking and locked; changing it takes your explicit request.
terms.engineer: A record with an id, rule, reason, sources and platform tags. It can lock values, add code checks, settle questions and rule out options. Project ids start PRJ-.
terms.example: Your brand book says buttons use 6 px corners, so they always do.

terms.plain: A guess put in so the work can go on, marked for you to check later.
terms.designer: A stand-in answer for something only the owner knows, like audience or brand facts. It keeps work moving but must be confirmed and never shown as decided.
terms.engineer: set_by: assumed, via --set-by assumed (a leading "pending:" in --why maps here too). DESIGN.md Open Items and the final summary list every assumed path for confirmation.
terms.example: Audience set to office workers until you confirm.

terms.plain: A safe answer left in place for you, because no one got to that question.
terms.designer: A sourced default that stands because the question was never reached, or had one right answer. It goes in the stage summary so someone can revisit it.
terms.engineer: set_by: auto_default; unreached or mechanical questions need no command. init logs D-0001 this way; auto_default decisions logged with a value appear in DESIGN.md Open Items.
terms.example: You stopped early, so the icon size kept its default.

terms.plain: Means you picked this answer yourself.
terms.designer: The strongest status: the owner made this call. Treat it as intent, and raise any concern as a question rather than changing it.
terms.engineer: set_by: chosen, the default for engine.py set and pick when --set-by is omitted. Stored on the answer or dial record and in its decisions.md entry.
terms.example: You typed teal, so teal is chosen.

terms.plain: We gave you a suggested answer and you said yes to it.
terms.designer: The owner saw the recommended default and accepted it. It counts as decided, but tells reviewers the idea came from the recommendation.
terms.engineer: set_by: confirmed_default, recorded with engine.py set <path> <value> --set-by confirmed_default. A leading "default:" in --why is read as this status too.
terms.example: The suggestion was 16px text, and you said fine.

terms.plain: You said "you decide", so the AI made this choice for you.
terms.designer: The owner handed this call to the model. It still carries a reason, and it is listed at the next approval gate so the owner can review it.
terms.engineer: set_by: delegated, via engine.py set <path> <value> --set-by delegated --why "<model's reason>". Listed at the next gate and in DESIGN.md Open Items.
terms.example: You said pick any motion, so the AI chose calm motion.

terms.plain: A choice kept safe, so no one can change it without asking and unlocking it first.
terms.designer: Use it for what must not drift: brand hexes, accessibility floors, anything the owner fixes. Later sessions have to ask before touching it.
terms.engineer: A path with locked: true on its answer or dial record, or listed in state.json locks. engine.py set refuses it until it is unlocked, or --force with consent.
terms.example: The logo color is locked, so a new page cannot change it.

terms.plain: Taken from a site or file you shared as an example you like.
terms.designer: The value came from a reference you shared, measured for structure and quality only. Another brand's logo, exact hue or proprietary typeface is not copied.
terms.engineer: set_by: reference, with --source-ref <ref-id>; written by engine.py intake --accept or set --set-by reference. The ref id points into state.json references.
terms.example: Tight spacing taken from a site you admire.

terms.plain: An old choice that a newer one replaced, with both kept in the diary so you can see the change.
terms.designer: Nothing in the history is erased. When a decision changes, the old entry stays and the new one points back to it, so you can trace how the system grew.
terms.engineer: decisions.md is append-only: a later entry for the same path supersedes the earlier one and records supersedes: D-nnnn. The newest entry per path is the effective value.
terms.example: D-0009 replaces D-0002 when corners go from subtle to soft.

terms.plain: What a screen is for: selling something, getting work done, reading, or enjoying an experience.
terms.designer: Persuade, Operate, Read or Experience, set for each surface. It changes spacing, card use and big hero moments, not the brand.
terms.engineer: answers.Q-scope-06 fills context.surfaces with {name, mode}. The main surface sets raw.productType; any Persuade or Experience surface sets raw.marketingSurfaces. No dial moves.
terms.designer_says: surface mode: persuade, operate, read, experience
terms.example: A landing page is Persuade; the dashboard behind it is Operate.

terms.plain: Five lines at the top of your design file: your picture of it, color, shape, motion, and what to avoid.
terms.designer: A one-glance style brief in the Overview. The picture and the Never list are only ever the person's own; color, shape and motion repeat each section's opening sentence.
terms.engineer: Rendered into DESIGN.md's Overview by taste_card() in engine.py, from taste.brief (sketch --brief), taste.never and the taste index's red lines.
terms.example: In your words: "a quiet library at night". Never: gradients, emoji (your words).

terms.plain: A full write-up of one look you love, so your AI can make new pages that match it.
terms.designer: One look described in full: a picture, 5 to 7 principles with reasons, colour jobs and shares, type, components, motion, voice, a Never list and a live specimen.
terms.engineer: opendesigner-extract taste_index.py draft writes opendesigner/taste-indexes/<id>/: TASTE-INDEX.md, a CSS file of variables and specimen.html; use <id> --fonts exact|free makes the system follow it.
terms.example: Warm paper, near-black ink, one teal accent, a lot of empty space.

terms.plain: A small web page that shows each option as a real sample, so you can see it before you pick.
terms.designer: Show, then ask: a live sample of each option on real components (palette, type scale, spacing ruler, radius, elevation, motion, component sheet, option gallery) instead of a description.
terms.engineer: One of eight self-contained HTML files in assets/templates/, fed a JSON payload in its od-data script and filled from engine.py resolve; show.py opens a local copy.
terms.example: The radius page shows buttons with four corner sizes.

terms.plain: How much care a question gets: big choices get more time, and small ones get a quick yes.
terms.designer: Tells the model where to slow down. High-weight questions shape many others, so they get real options and a line on what else changes; low-weight ones get a quick default.
terms.engineer: The weight field (high, medium, low) in questions.json: high means fan-out 5+ or a Quick question, medium fan-out 2-4 or owner inputs, low otherwise, per pacing.json.
terms.example: Brand personality is high weight; icon stroke is low.

terms.plain: The list of problems the checker found: ones you must fix and ones worth a look, each with its rule.
terms.designer: Tells you what blocks shipping (errors, like text contrast under 4.5:1 or targets under 24px) and what needs judgment (warnings), each citing its rule and source.
terms.engineer: Printed by validate or build, or JSON with --json: items with severity (error, warn, info), category, rule, where, measured, threshold, evidence and fix; plus lowest ratios and a summary.
terms.example: Error: body text on gray is 3.9 to 1, below 4.5.

terms.plain: The second step of detail, with one quick screen for each main part of your design.
terms.designer: Zoom level 1: one short screen per foundation (style, density, color use, text, corners, depth, motion, where files live). About 8 questions and 8 minutes.
terms.engineer: Zoom level 1: the eight questions in pacing.json zoom1. Stored as state.json zoom.<area> = "broad", or inferred from 1-2 decisions in the area.
terms.example: One screen picks corners, the next picks depth.

terms.plain: The third step of detail: you pick one part, like color, and set it with real numbers.
terms.designer: Zoom level 2: one area at a time, such as color ramps, roles and contrast, with real values. Take only the areas that matter for your product.
terms.engineer: Zoom level 2: an area's level-2 questions in stage order, then engine.py generate. Stored as zoom.<area> = "defined", or inferred from 3-5 decisions in that area.
terms.example: Zoom into color to set exact shades and contrast.

terms.plain: The deepest step, where every small part and button is worked out in full.
terms.designer: Zoom level 3: the fine print of each area plus blocks, components and patterns, built from the system's values rather than from scratch.
terms.engineer: Zoom level 3: questions tagged zoom 3, from stages/NN-*.detailed.md. Stored as zoom.<area> = "detailed", or inferred from 6 or more decisions or any override in that area.
terms.example: Every button state, such as hover and disabled, is set.

terms.plain: A slider for how much the app looks like your brand, or like the phone it runs on.
terms.designer: Native (0): system font and components, brand only in accents. Brand-led (100): custom face, brand color on large surfaces, custom components. Navigation, back and sheets always stay native.
terms.engineer: Posture dial, default 50. Sets guidance params type.faceSuggestion, brand color placement, nativeShare (1.0 at 0, 0.8 at 50, 0 at 100) and content.voiceGuidance; behavior.navigationNative stays true.
terms.example: Fluent's 80/20 guidance: reuse native components most of the time.

terms.plain: A slider for how much color the app uses, from all gray to bright and bold.
terms.designer: Low keeps the palette near gray with one accent; high raises accent chroma, adds secondary and tertiary accents from 60 and tints surfaces. Spend strong color on small, meaningful elements.
terms.engineer: Character dial 0-100, default 50. Accent chroma for color.accent.* (HCT 0, 10, 34, 48, max), scheme variant (monochrome to vibrant) and accent count (1, or 3 from 60).
terms.example: Material's scheme variants run from Monochrome to Vibrant along this dial.

terms.plain: A slider for how much fits on one screen, from roomy and calm to tight and packed.
terms.designer: Spacious (0) reads calm: 16px+ body, 48px controls. Compact (100) reads serious and efficient: 14px body (13 at 90+), 32px controls. Hit areas never shrink.
terms.engineer: Posture dial 0-100. Drives type.baseSize.web (19-13), size.control.md (48/40/32), size.icon.default (24/20/16) and density context; size.target.min never changes.
terms.example: GOV.UK's 19px body sits near 0; Polaris's 13px near 90.

terms.plain: A slider for how much parts seem to lift off the page, from flat to deep.
terms.designer: Each band is a different model: borders only, ring plus faint shadow, tonal layers, shadow ladder, then glass materials with a solid fallback. Dark mode lifts raised surfaces by lightness.
terms.engineer: Character dial 0-100, default 40. The elevation model breaks at 15, 35, 55 and 80; light shadow alpha (color.shadow.key) runs 0.08-0.24; dark mode lifts raised surfaces.
terms.example: GOV.UK uses borders only; Apple's Liquid Glass sits at the deep end.

terms.plain: A slider for how lively the app feels, from calm to bouncy and bright.
terms.designer: Calm (0) uses no-overshoot springs, shorter durations (0.8x), lighter headings and recessive navigation; energetic (100) adds bounce, 1.2x longer medium moves, more saturation and heavier headings.
terms.engineer: Character dial 0-100, default 50. Sets spatial spring damping ratio (1.0-0.6) and stiffness (700-380) in motion.spring.spatial.*, motion.easing.standard and a duration multiplier (0.8-1.2).
terms.example: Material 3's standard spring damps at 0.9; its expressive one at 0.8.

terms.plain: A slider for how much the app shows off, from quiet and plain to bold and loud.
terms.designer: Productive (0) keeps attention on the task; expressive (100) adds emphasis: a bigger type scale, more weights, hero moments, brand-colored chrome, visible containers and motion throughout.
terms.engineer: Posture dial 0-100, default 50. Drives type.ratio 1.2/1.25/1.333, type.weightCount 2-4, emphasis.heroMoments, layout.containment, brand color role and expressive motion scope (resolve params).
terms.example: Above 66, Material-style emphasized type is requested; it is not generated yet.

terms.plain: A slider for how round the corners are, from sharp boxes to soft pill shapes.
terms.designer: Sets the default control radius and everything derived from it: container and overlay radii, nested radii, focus-ring radius, icon corners and caps. Benchmark median is 6px.
terms.engineer: Character dial 0-100, default 50. radius.control bands: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16px, full (pill) at 93+. Sets icon corner style and cap shape (resolve params).
terms.example: Carbon sits at 0px corners; Material 3 uses full pill buttons.

terms.plain: A slider for how cool and formal or warm and friendly the grays and the wording feel.
terms.designer: Cool tints neutrals blue (slate) with title case and firmer borders; warm tints them toward stone or taupe, softens borders, uses sentence case and contractions. Brand hue never moves.
terms.engineer: Character dial 0-100. OKLCH neutral tint (chroma, hue) of color.neutral.*: slate (0.046, 257) at 0, gray at 50, taupe (0.021, 43) at 100; plus border and casing rules.
terms.designer_says: cool slate to warm taupe neutrals
terms.example: Cool end: GOV.UK writes "cannot". Warm end: "can't" and "we".

terms.plain: The facts you gather first: who it is for, where it runs, how the brand feels, and what limits apply.
terms.designer: The brief behind every visual choice: purpose, audience, platforms, devices, brand personality and hard limits. Settle these first, because they constrain more later decisions than any other input.
terms.engineer: Step-0 and step-1 inputs in the decision graph, kept in state.json (context.*, raw.*, answers), not tokens. The brand personality card alone constrains 15 later decisions.
terms.example: A calm banking app for the web, iPhone and Android.

terms.plain: What the brand brings: how it feels, how it ties to its ads, and how bold the app may be.
terms.designer: What the brand brings: its personality, how the expressive identity (logo, campaign color, display type) relates to the productive product UI, and how much expression the product allows.
terms.engineer: Not tokens: answers.Q-brand-01 sliders become macros that offset dials, answers.Q-brand-04 records expressiveness, and raw.marketingSurfaces widens display type. An expressive mode axis is planned.

terms.plain: How bold the brand may get in the app, and how many showy moments it is allowed.
terms.designer: How much brand expression the product allows. Default, Material's rule: productive everywhere plus one or two hero moments with expressive type, shape or motion, kept for key interactions.
terms.engineer: Planned, not generated yet: expressive variants as a mode or parallel set, such as font.display.emphasized (proposed), shape.corner.expressive.* (proposed), motion.spring.expressive.* (proposed), from DC-L06-03.
terms.example: A bold, springy success screen after payment; calm screens everywhere else.

terms.plain: Whether the pages that sell the app and the app itself share one set of design rules.
terms.designer: Whether marketing (expressive) and product (productive) surfaces share one system or run separately. Default: one system, productive by default, expressive opt-in; split only when separate teams own separate surfaces.
terms.engineer: Planned, not generated yet: a layer mode axis (productive | expressive), not duplicate tokens. Today Energy picks Carbon productive (0-33) or expressive (67+) curves for motion.easing.enter and .exit.

terms.plain: A few sliders for how the brand feels, like fun or serious, that guide most later choices.
terms.designer: Brand traits as slider positions, such as playful to serious; OpenDesigner uses seven. The most influential input: each pair nudges concrete foundation dials. The style screen then shows directions.
terms.engineer: Not a design token. answers.Q-brand-01 stores seven slider positions; six become macros in state.json, such as {id: playful, strength: 0.4}, that offset the dials; one sets Energy.

terms.plain: Limits you do not get to pick, such as the law, your design app plan, and which languages you need.
terms.designer: Limits that are not taste: the design tool plan, the legal accessibility target, supported locales and scripts. Ask for the Figma plan first; it caps modes per collection.
terms.engineer: Not tokens: context.constraints lists limits and exports.figmaPlan the Figma plan. Figma caps modes per collection (Professional 10, Organization 20); validate warns and the Figma export splits bigger collections.
terms.designer_says: hard limits: tool plan, legal, locales

terms.plain: A look through your screens today to list every button, color and size you use.
terms.designer: Screenshot every unique pattern and audit colors, type and spacing in current products. Its main value is shared vocabulary and buy-in, so do it by hand even with automated data.
terms.engineer: Not stored; audit.findings[] is proposed. css_scan.py counts declared colors, sizes and radii; engine.py review lists hard-coded values. Inventory per platform: sheet, modal and dialog differ.
terms.example: Finding many slightly different grays across your products.

terms.plain: The places your app must run, like the web, iPhones or Android phones.
terms.designer: The operating systems served. Platform choice drives units, native type, target sizes, materials and navigation. OpenDesigner defaults to web only; research suggests adding iOS and Android phones from day one.
terms.engineer: Stored as raw.platforms; no DTCG type. A platform resolver modifier is planned, not generated; today each platform gets its own export, and pointer media queries set size.target.min.

terms.plain: Which kinds of screens get full care, like phones and laptops, and which get only the basics.
terms.designer: Pick which device classes get full design (phone, tablet and foldable, desktop) and which get foundations only. A class is first-class when a core task happens there.
terms.engineer: Planned, not generated: a device-class resolver modifier (handheld, wrist, desk, lean-back, vehicle, spatial), separate from platform since Android spans phones, Wear, TV and Auto. Recorded as answers.Q-plat-02.

terms.plain: The oldest phone or computer software your app still has to work on.
terms.designer: The oldest OS versions supported and the design-language generation targeted. Default: support current and previous major versions, design for the current language, let older ones fall back to native.
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-plat-09; OpenDesigner emits no version-gated values. Prefer runtime fallbacks, for example dynamic color falling back to the brand scheme below Android 12.

terms.plain: How much your app should look like each phone's own style, or look the same on all of them.
terms.designer: Native-first, brand-first or coherent hybrid. Default hybrid: share what users see as the brand (accent, headline type, icons, voice) and use each platform's own navigation, sheets, pickers and fields.
terms.engineer: Not a token: answers.Q-plat-05 and the Brand presence dial; below 50, native platforms keep their body size. Exports emit literal colors; mapping to label or onSurface is planned.
terms.example: Brand-blue buttons, but the phone's own back gesture and date picker.

terms.plain: Which parts stay the same on every device, like brand colors and names, and which parts change.
terms.designer: Choose whether platforms share tokens, component specs or only principles. Default: share the what (brand hue, role names, spacing numbers, voice); adapt the how (materials, target minimums, navigation containers).
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-plat-07. Every export shares one token set with the same names; only target sizes vary by input. Per-platform overrides and shared component specs are planned.
terms.designer_says: share the what, adapt the how
terms.code_name: answers.Q-plat-07; one token set, same names

terms.plain: The coding tools your team builds the app with, which decide what form the design files take.
terms.designer: The toolkits products are built with. Native toolkits get new OS looks first; Flutter or Compose Multiplatform suit brand-first products that accept a lag behind OS visual changes.
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-plat-08; it does not change exports yet. build writes SwiftUI, Compose, CSS and Tailwind files; React Native objects and flutter/class.dart are not generated.

terms.plain: The list of which apps and people your first version will serve, and which ones it will leave out.
terms.designer: Name the products, audiences and technologies version 1 serves, and what it will not serve. Scope to the pilot; add platforms only when a real product needs them.
terms.engineer: Stored in state.json as raw.platforms, for example ["web", "ios"], and context.scope {in, out}. Today build writes every export (CSS, Tailwind, Figma, Paper, Swift, Compose, DTCG) regardless.

terms.plain: The choice to use a ready-made kit, change one to fit, or build your own, and how strict to be.
terms.designer: Decide whether to adopt an existing system, adapt a themeable base, or create your own, and how strict, modular and centralized it will be.
terms.engineer: Not tokens: answers.Q-scope-05 (adopt, adapt or create) and answers.Q-gov-01 (strict or loose) in state.json; components.base names a base library. Nothing acts on them yet.
terms.example: A small team adapts a headless base and puts its effort into tokens and docs.

terms.plain: The rules that say what good means, before anyone picks a color or a size.
terms.designer: Defines what good means before any value is picked: team design principles, UX behavior rules from laws and heuristics, and visual principles. It decides whether the product works.
terms.engineer: Parent of prin.design, prin.ux and prin.visual. Not tokens: principles in state.json holds ranked statements; UX and visual rules live in the formulas or engine.py validate.

terms.plain: A short, ranked list of beliefs a team uses to settle ties when two good ideas clash.
terms.designer: 3-5 ranked statements that break ties when good options conflict, each naming the value it outranks. Avoid words every product claims, like simple; test each: would this screen pass?
terms.engineer: Not tokens: principles in state.json is an ordered list of statements; order is rank, and DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md print them as tie-breakers.
terms.example: Clarity over density: when unsure, show fewer items per screen.

terms.plain: Content in neat boxes of different sizes, like the parts of a lunch box.
terms.designer: Tiles of two or three spans in one grid with one gap; one idea per tile, the hero tile largest. A layout that borrows its look from another style.
terms.engineer: CSS grid with grid-column and grid-row spans; Q-dir-04 containers. Keep DOM order equal to reading order (WCAG 1.3.2) and reflow to one column.

terms.plain: Puffy, round shapes that look made of soft clay or toy plastic.
terms.designer: Large radius, a soft outer shadow plus light and dark inner shadows, pastel color and 3D clay art. Friendly and cute; keep product controls calmer.
terms.engineer: No preset of its own: start from soft, then raise roundness above 80 and colorfulness. Inner shadows are not generated yet (proposed); 3D art is an asset (Q-img-06).

terms.plain: Looks like a comic book, with thick ink outlines, bright flat colors, dots and speech bubbles.
terms.designer: Black outlines, primary colors, halftone dot shading, speech balloons and burst shapes; pop art is its gallery cousin. Keep hand lettering to short labels.
terms.engineer: Start from the neobrutal preset with colorfulness above 88. Halftone is a radial-gradient dot pattern; drawings are assets (Q-img-04, opendesigner-illustrate).

terms.plain: Pages that read like a good magazine: big titles, calm text and large photos.
terms.designer: Serif display headlines, dramatic size jumps (1.333 or more), 60-75 character lines, pull quotes and thin rules. For reading products and long content.
terms.engineer: Q-type-03 serif, Q-dir-03 dramatic (type ratio 1.333) and Q-dir-04 lines. Body text stays 16px or larger; limit lines with max-width: 65ch.

terms.plain: Plain solid colors with no shadows, no shine and no texture.
terms.designer: Solid fills, simple icons, hierarchy from color and size. Flat 2.0 brings subtle shadows back. Keep strong signs of what to click, or people search longer.
terms.engineer: Depth 0-15 builds the borders model with no shadows. The default flat2 preset (Q-dir-01) sets Depth 30: a ring plus a faint shadow.

terms.plain: See-through panels that look like frosted glass, so you see a blur of what is behind them.
terms.designer: Translucent fill, background blur and a thin light edge over rich content. Use it on bars, sheets and menus, never on reading surfaces, and give it a solid twin.
terms.engineer: Q-dir-01 glass, or Depth above 80, builds the materials model: material.glass.blur (24px), color.surface.glass and color.surface.glass-fallback. Web uses backdrop-filter.

terms.plain: A fine speckle over colors, like old film or printed paper.
terms.designer: Fine noise at 3-8% strength over fills and gradients. It warms flat color and hides gradient banding; keep it off body text and keep it still.
terms.engineer: An SVG feTurbulence image on a pseudo-element with mix-blend-mode: overlay. Not a token yet (proposed); record it with the H-motif hook (Q-img-07).

terms.plain: Soft clouds of a few colors that melt into each other, like the northern lights.
terms.designer: Three to five colors blending in many directions, often blurred and slowly moving. Marketing and brand moments only, never on buttons or forms.
terms.engineer: Stacked radial-gradient layers or blurred shapes, interpolated in OKLab. DTCG gradient tokens hold stops only; the engine does not generate gradients yet (proposed).

terms.plain: Bright flat colors with thick black lines and hard black shadows, like stickers.
terms.designer: Thick borders, a solid 4px offset shadow, 2-3 bold colors, 24-32px padding and a quirky display face over a neutral body face. Loud and indie.
terms.engineer: Q-dir-01 neo-brutalist selects the neobrutal preset (roundness 5, depth 0, colorfulness 80). Thick borders and the offset shadow need overrides of border.width.default and elevation.raised.

terms.plain: Soft buttons that look pushed up out of the page, or pressed in, all one color.
terms.designer: Same-color surfaces with paired light and dark soft shadows. Tactile but vague: edges usually fail 3:1, so every control needs an added border or fill.
terms.engineer: Q-dir-01 soft selects the soft preset (roundness 80, colorfulness 20) and the lint warns neumorphic-preset. Paired and inset shadows are not generated yet (proposed).

terms.plain: Screens that copy real objects and materials, like a record player, a tape or wood.
