terms.engineer: Emitted DTCG groups: color, font, text, space, size, radius, border, elevation, opacity, motion, focus and icon. Shadow, z-index and breakpoint groups are not generated; native uses elevation and size classes.

terms.plain: The form design values take inside each kind of app code, like a web page or a phone app.
terms.designer: The form tokens take in each platform's code. On the web: CSS custom properties, media queries for user preferences, container queries for components, viewport breakpoints only for page layout.
terms.engineer: OpenDesigner writes build/css/tokens.css, tailwind/theme.css, swift/DesignTokens.swift and compose/DesignTokens.kt. Web themes follow prefers-color-scheme with a [data-theme] override; type uses rem. No Flutter output.
terms.example: --ds-color-text-primary in CSS, a DsColors class in Compose.

terms.plain: The switches that change values in one go, like light and dark, or roomy and tight.
terms.designer: The axes along which values switch, such as color scheme, contrast, density or brand. OpenDesigner generates light and dark, three densities and reduced motion; no contrast or brand modes yet.
terms.engineer: DTCG Resolver modifiers with contexts (theme, density, motion); Figma collections and modes. Outputs multiply, so keep axes few, and orthogonal so no two set the same token. Primitives stay single-valued.
terms.example: Page background is white in light mode and near-black in dark mode.

terms.plain: The rules for how saved choices get their names, so you can guess a name and find it.
terms.designer: The grammar that makes token names predictable: category, property, concept, variant, state. Theme and brand never appear in semantic names, because they are modes.
terms.engineer: category.property.concept.variant, every segment lowercase kebab-case, state joined by a hyphen: color.bg.accent.bold-hover. CSS adds the prefix (--ds-color-bg-accent-bold-hover); Swift and Compose use camelCase.

terms.plain: How the basic values get named, like accent 9 for a shade or space 16 for a 16 pixel gap.
terms.designer: Research favors hue plus a numeric step for color. OpenDesigner names ramps by role and step (accent 9), space by pixel value (16), and keeps t-shirt sizes for semantic tokens.
terms.engineer: Emitted: color.accent.light.9 (color: role, mode, step) and space.16 (dimension, named by px). Hue names such as color.blue.600 (proposed) are not generated. Avoid ordinal scales.

terms.plain: How one design gets a new look, for a new brand or a customer, without being rebuilt.
terms.designer: How the system is re-skinned: a few inputs generate a theme, several brands share one system, and white-label customers change a limited set of values.
terms.engineer: Parent of tok.themes.generator, .brands and .whitelabel. Today inputs such as raw.brandColor generate the theme; a re-skin overrides primitives through state.json overrides. Semantic names never change.

terms.plain: How a few brands share one set of parts: they work the same, but colors and fonts change.
terms.designer: Fixed across brands: anatomy, behavior, semantic names, status meanings. Flexible: brand color, typeface, logo, imagery. Radius, density and motion flex with care. Build as if a second brand will come.
terms.engineer: Planned, not generated yet: a brand resolver modifier or Figma extended collection whose contexts re-point a brandable set, such as color.accent.* and font.family.display; semantic names stay fixed.

terms.plain: A few brand choices, like the main color, from which a whole look is worked out for you.
terms.designer: The few brand knobs a whole theme is computed from. Default three: brand or accent color, neutral base or temperature, and contrast. A warmer gray alone shifts personality.
terms.engineer: Inputs are raw.brandColor, raw.neutralBase and raw.contrastTarget in state.json, with the Warmth dial; engine.py generate derives the color.accent.* and color.neutral.* ramps in OKLCH.

terms.plain: The short list of things other companies may change to make the app their own, like logo and color.
terms.designer: What external customers may change in a white-label product. Default: brand color and logo; font and radius only with previews and validation. Everything else is derived.
terms.engineer: Today the accent ramps derive from one input, raw.brandColor. Proposed tenant inputs: tenant.color.brand (proposed), tenant.logo (proposed), optionally tenant.font.display (proposed); all else derives.

terms.plain: Layers of names, from raw values like a blue shade up to names that say what the blue is for.
terms.designer: Primitives hold raw values; semantic tokens say what a value is for and are where theming happens; optional component tokens, not generated yet, let one component restyle on its own.
terms.engineer: Semantic color.bg.accent.bold = "{color.accent.light.9}", a primitive; planned component token button.primary.bg (proposed) would alias it. Aliases must share a type and never cycle.
terms.example: Accent shade 9, then accent background, then a primary button background.

terms.plain: The set way each kind of choice is written down, such as colors, sizes, fonts and motion.
terms.designer: How each kind of value is written: color, dimensions, typography, shadow and border, motion, layout. It decides what survives the trip into Figma and each platform.
terms.engineer: The 13 DTCG 2025.10 types. Gaps include springs, string, boolean, percentages and assets; springs go in $extensions on a transition token with a cubic-bezier fallback.

terms.plain: How each color is written in the file so every tool shows the same shade.
terms.designer: Which color space colors are stored in, with a hex fallback. Author in OKLCH or sRGB, send sRGB to Figma, and use P3 only for vivid brand colors.
terms.engineer: $type color with colorSpace (such as oklch), components, optional alpha and a hex fallback. Figma imports sRGB and HSL only, so an OKLCH master also exports sRGB.

terms.plain: What unit sizes are saved in, like pixels, and how they change for each kind of screen.
terms.designer: Which unit sizes are stored in, and how they become pt on iOS, dp on Android, epx on Windows and rem on the web. Storing px keeps Figma import lossless.
terms.engineer: $type dimension {value: 16, unit: "px"}; DTCG allows only px and rem. OpenDesigner exports px 1:1 as pt and dp, and CSS font sizes as rem.

terms.plain: Extra things the shared file has no slot for, like bouncy motion or very bright colors, kept in side notes.
terms.designer: Values the standard format cannot hold: springs, text and yes-or-no values, icon and font references, aspect ratios and rules. OpenDesigner keeps builder settings like preset in state.json.
terms.engineer: Today $extensions.opendesigner holds springs, P3 values, provenance and evidence; builder settings (preset, macros) live in state.json and opendesigner.meta.json. String and boolean extensions are not generated.

terms.plain: How screen widths and column grids are saved, so the layout changes as the screen grows.
terms.designer: How breakpoints, grids and layout guides are stored. Research default: a three-mode breakpoint collection driving spacing and guides, plus grid auto layout. OpenDesigner does not generate breakpoints yet.
terms.engineer: No DTCG breakpoint type. Not generated: layout.grid.columns (proposed; 4, 8 or 12), layout.gutter (proposed), layout.margin (proposed). Figma grid auto layout maps to CSS grid.

terms.plain: How the speed and feel of movement on screen is saved, like how long a slide takes.
terms.designer: How durations, easings and springs are stored. OpenDesigner emits eight durations and four easings, mirrored as Figma timing and easing variables with a reduced-motion mode. Research suggests 3-5 durations.
terms.engineer: DTCG duration, cubicBezier and transition, such as motion.duration.short = {value: 150, unit: "ms"}; springs stay in $extensions until DTCG adds a type.

terms.plain: How shadows and outlines are saved so both design tools and code draw them the same.
terms.designer: How shadows, borders and elevation are stored so design and code match. Figma effect styles bind color and offset to variables, so dark mode can swap the shadow color.
terms.engineer: elevation.floating is a DTCG shadow array of ring, key and ambient layers. Borders are border.width.* dimensions, not border or strokeStyle composites. Android and iOS shadows need custom transforms.

terms.plain: How text settings like font, size and weight are saved: as one bundle, as single parts, or both.
terms.designer: Whether type is stored as bundled styles, separate values, or both. Default both: atomic font values plus role-based composites, mirrored in Figma as text styles bound to variables.
terms.engineer: Atomic fontFamily, fontWeight and dimension tokens (line heights in px) plus composites like text.body.md. Figma lacks composite variables, so composites become text styles bound to variables.

terms.plain: The parts an app is made of, like buttons and menus, built once and used again.
terms.designer: Reusable UI elements with defined anatomy, variants and states, styled from the system's tokens. OpenDesigner's catalog lists 64 canonical components in ten categories, benchmarked across 10 systems.
terms.engineer: Catalog entries C01-C64 list anatomy, props, states, the APG pattern and token families used. No component tokens are generated yet; components use semantic tokens directly.
terms.example: A Button, a Dialog and a Card are three components.

terms.plain: Parts you tap or click to make something happen, like buttons.
terms.designer: Components that trigger actions: button, icon button, floating action button, split button, button group, toggle button and toolbar. Their emphasis and placement signal what users should do next.
terms.engineer: APG patterns: Button (Enter and Space activate), toggle Button with aria-pressed, Menu Button with aria-haspopup, and Toolbar with a roving tabindex. Natives: SwiftUI Button, UIKit UIButton, Compose Button.
terms.example: Save, Share and a plus button that adds an item.

terms.term: Button hierarchy, content and destructive treatment
terms.plain: How many kinds of button there are, which one stands out, and how a Delete button looks.
terms.designer: Four emphasis levels plus danger, one primary per view, placed after the last field. Sentence-case verb labels with an optional leading icon; solid danger only in the confirmation step.
terms.engineer: Semantic tokens color.bg.action.primary with color.text.on-action, and color.bg.danger.bold for destructive; button component tokens are not generated yet. APG Button; SwiftUI destructive role.
terms.example: One filled Save button beside a plain-text Cancel button.

terms.plain: The switches and knobs on a part, like size or style, that people use to set it up.
terms.designer: How a component is configured in Figma: variants for state, size and type, booleans for optional icons, text properties for labels, instance swap for fixed icons, slots for flexible content.
terms.engineer: Props for leaf components like Button; compound parts (Menu.Trigger, Menu.Item) for containers like Dialog. Figma slots map to React children, and booleans bind only to layer visibility.
terms.example: A Button with a size setting and an optional icon.

terms.plain: A short write-up of what starts a small action, what it does, and what you see or feel.
terms.designer: Each interactive component documents Saffer's four parts: trigger, rules, feedback, and loops and modes, plus its state list. This keeps press, hover, success and failure feedback consistent across the product.
terms.engineer: Implement the spec as a state machine, as Ark UI does; store trigger, rules, feedback, loops and modes as structured component docs. DTCG has no behavior type.
terms.example: Pull to refresh: the pull is the trigger, the spinner is the feedback.

terms.plain: Parts that group things, like cards, sections that open and close, and dividing lines.
terms.designer: Components that group content: card, accordion, divider and carousel. They set how content chunks read, whether by fill, outline or shadow, and how much stays hidden until opened.
terms.engineer: APG Accordion (a heading wrapping a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls), Disclosure, and Carousel (rotation stop control first in tab order). Natives: SwiftUI DisclosureGroup; Compose Card, ElevatedCard, OutlinedCard.
terms.example: A help page where each question opens to show its answer.

terms.plain: How a card stands apart from the page: a light fill, a thin border, or a shadow.
terms.designer: Tinted fill feels soft and works in dark mode, outline feels crisp and flat, shadow adds depth. Use fill or outline for static cards, elevation only for floating things.
terms.engineer: Tokens: color.surface.raised, color.border.subtle, radius.container and elevation.raised. Interactive cards bounded only by a border need 3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11).
terms.example: Cards on a pale gray page, each with a thin outline.

terms.plain: Parts that show facts and people, like lists, tables and small photos of users.
terms.designer: Components that present data and people: list, table, avatar, and text and heading. Density, row height and type roles decide how scannable a screen of data feels.
terms.engineer: APG Table for static data, Grid for interactive or editable cells, Treegrid for nested rows, Listbox for selectable lists. Natives: SwiftUI List and Table, UIKit UITableView.
terms.example: A table of orders with a small photo of each customer.

terms.plain: A small picture or letters that stand for a person, team or AI helper.
terms.designer: Sizes from 16 to 64 on a 4/8 rhythm. Circle means person, square means team or organization, and a third shape marks AI agents when humans and AI mix.
terms.engineer: radius.person aliases radius.full (9999px); avatar sizes 16 to 64, avatar.size.* (proposed), are not generated yet. Add alt text when no name sits beside it.
terms.designer_says: circle for people, square for teams
terms.example: A round photo for a person, a square logo for a team.

terms.plain: If one set of parts fits phones and laptops, or if watches and TVs get their own.
terms.designer: One component set covers phone, tablet, desktop and web through context modes; watch and TV get small separate libraries because their input changes, not only their size.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: a context modifier so shared names like color.bg.action.primary resolve per device, and namespaces like wrist.tile.* (proposed) for device-only parts. Car uses system templates.
terms.example: Google ships separate Compose libraries for Wear and TV.

terms.plain: Parts that tell you what is going on, like a warning box, a loading bar or a red dot.
terms.designer: Components that report status, progress or results: alert or banner, toast, progress bar, spinner, skeleton, empty state, badge and AI indicators. Four status colors map info, success, warning and error.
terms.engineer: APG Alert (role alert, no focus move); toasts use a status live region on color.bg.inverse. Status: color.bg.danger.subtle, color.text.danger, likewise info, success, warning.
terms.example: A green banner saying your changes were saved.

terms.plain: Extra parts for AI features, like a label that says AI made this, and chat bubbles.
terms.designer: An optional module: AI label and AI button variant first, chat components only for conversational products. A distinct AI accent aids recognition but can compete with the primary color.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: color.ai.* (proposed) accent or gradient tokens. Examples: Carbon AI label, Spectrum 2 genai variant, shadcn Message. Stream text into polite live regions.
terms.example: A small AI tag next to a summary the app wrote.

terms.plain: Picking what the parts are built on: a kit with no looks, a kit with looks, or the phone's own.
terms.designer: Picks the base under your components. Headless libraries leave every visual choice to your tokens, styled libraries arrive with a look to re-theme, and native controls inherit the platform's look.
terms.engineer: Suggested for React web: shadcn/ui on Base UI or React Aria; multi-framework: Ark UI or web components; mobile: SwiftUI and Compose controls themed with tokens. Recorded in components.base.
terms.example: A React app styling shadcn/ui components with its own tokens.

terms.plain: Parts where you type or pick something, like a text box, a date picker or a file upload.
terms.designer: Components for entering data, from text fields and selects to date pickers, file uploads and one-time codes. Field style, label placement and validation decide how easy forms feel.
terms.engineer: Native inputs plus aria-describedby for help and errors and aria-invalid; APG Combobox for suggestions, Listbox or select-only Combobox for Select, Spinbutton for number fields. Compose TextField, SwiftUI TextField.
terms.example: An email box, a country dropdown and a birthday picker.

terms.term: Form field style and label placement
terms.plain: How a text box looks, with a full border, a shaded fill or a line, and where its name sits.
terms.designer: Outlined reads crisp, filled reads soft and app-like, underlined is minimal but low in affordance. Default: outlined fields with top labels; mark whichever of required or optional is rarer.
terms.engineer: Tokens: color.border.input (3:1), color.border.focus, color.border.danger, text.label.* for labels; input component tokens are not generated yet. Every input needs a programmatic label.
terms.example: A box with a border and its label, Email, sitting above it.

terms.plain: Choosing which parts to make first, and when to add more later.
terms.designer: Version 1's library size. The default is the 25 core components the engine starts with; extended ones, such as date pickers, come when two or more products ask.
terms.engineer: The list lives in components.inventory in state.json; each included component must implement its APG pattern. Per-component token namespaces such as button.* (proposed) are not generated yet.
terms.example: Buttons and checkboxes in version 1; a color picker later.

terms.plain: Hidden helper parts that space things out and help people who have the screen read aloud.
terms.designer: Box, stack and grid primitives expose spacing, color and radius as props so layouts stay on scale. The app shell and accessibility utilities, like visually hidden text, sit here too.
terms.engineer: Box, Stack, Inline and Grid take spacing tokens as props; the app shell uses APG Landmarks and Window Splitter; utilities include Radix Visually Hidden, Portal and Slot.
terms.example: A Stack that puts the same gap between every card.

terms.plain: Parts that show icons and pictures at the right size and shape.
terms.designer: Components that render icons and images, such as thumbnails. They keep icon sizes, image corners and aspect ratios on the system's scales instead of hand-set values.
terms.engineer: C60 Icon consumes icon size, stroke and color tokens; C61 Image consumes radius and surface tokens plus CSS aspect-ratio. Radix ships Accessible Icon and Aspect Ratio.
terms.designer_says: icons and images on system scales
terms.example: A trash-can icon and a square product photo.

terms.plain: Parts that help you move around an app, like tabs, links and a bar of icons at the bottom.
terms.designer: Components for moving between places: link, tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination, bottom navigation bar, navigation rail, sidebar, app bar, tree view and steps. The container follows screen size and destination count.
terms.engineer: Use links inside a nav landmark with aria-current, never the menu role. APG patterns: Tabs (tablist, tab, tabpanel), Breadcrumb, Tree View. Natives: SwiftUI TabView and NavigationSplitView, Compose NavigationBar and NavigationRail.
terms.example: Home, Search and Profile tabs along the bottom of a phone app.

terms.plain: Parts that pop up over the page, like tips, menus and boxes that ask you something.
terms.designer: Components that appear above the page: tooltip, popover, dialog, confirmation dialog, sheet or drawer, menu and command palette. Use modal ones only when blocking the page has a clear benefit.
terms.engineer: APG Dialog (Modal): focus moves inside and is trapped, Escape closes, focus returns to the invoker, with role dialog and aria-modal. Also Alert Dialog, Menu Button and Tooltip.
terms.example: A box asking Delete this file? with Delete and Cancel buttons.

terms.plain: Whether an app uses the phone's own buttons in its brand color, or draws its own.
terms.designer: System controls feel native and update with the OS, such as Liquid Glass; custom ones keep brand shape but can look out of place. Restyle color and label, not shape.
terms.engineer: Default: tint SwiftUI, UIKit and Compose controls with the accent token, custom controls on web. System controls carry VoiceOver and TalkBack roles; custom ones must supply them.
terms.example: An iOS toggle switch tinted in the brand's green.

terms.plain: Parts for making a choice, like check boxes, on-off switches and sliders.
terms.designer: Components for choosing among options: checkbox, radio group, switch, slider, segmented control and chip. Pick by task: switches apply instantly, radios pick one, checkboxes pick many, chips filter.
terms.engineer: APG Checkbox (aria-checked true, false or mixed), Radio Group (arrow keys move and select), Switch (role switch) and Slider (aria-valuenow). Natives: SwiftUI Toggle and Slider, Compose Checkbox, Switch, RadioButton.
terms.code_name: APG Checkbox, Radio Group, Switch, Slider
terms.example: A switch that turns dark mode on or off.

terms.plain: How a part looks when you point at it, press it, pick it, or it cannot be used.
terms.designer: Each component's looks: enabled, hover, focus-visible, pressed, selected, disabled, loading, error. Hover and press step one or two shades along the ramp; selected and error get explicit colors.
terms.engineer: DTCG has no state semantics; states become a name suffix such as color.bg.action.primary-hover or .primary-pressed. Define all states once; each context renders the subset its inputs trigger.
terms.example: A button shows a ring around it when reached with the Tab key.

terms.plain: What to do with a button that cannot work right now: fade it, hide it, or explain why.
terms.designer: Faded controls signal 'not now' but can hide why. The default never disables submit: it checks fields on blur, summarizes errors on submit, and explains when an action cannot run.
terms.engineer: Use aria-disabled, as APG recommends; it stays focusable, while disabled controls leave the tab order. Tokens: color.text.disabled, or opacity.disabled.content and .container. WCAG exempts them from contrast.
terms.example: A Save button that stays clickable and says what is missing.

terms.plain: How a part shows it is busy, like a spinning wheel or gray boxes where things will load.
terms.designer: Choose a spinner, a skeleton that previews the layout, or a loading button. Delay spinners about 1 s, use skeletons for first page loads, and keep loading buttons focusable.
terms.engineer: A delay token such as loading.delay (proposed) = 1000ms (DTCG duration); announce state through a 4.1.3 status message. Natives: UIKit UIActivityIndicatorView, Compose LoadingIndicator. S2 isPending keeps focus.
terms.example: A Save button showing a small spinner while it saves.

terms.plain: How the app shows which tab, row or item you picked, using a mark as well as a color.
terms.designer: Mark the chosen tab, row, chip or navigation item with an indicator plus color, never color alone. In action-dense products, save brand primary for actions.
terms.engineer: Expose aria-selected, aria-current or aria-pressed per pattern. Tokens: color.bg.accent.subtle, color.text.accent and border.width.selected; the indicator needs 3:1 contrast where it conveys state.
terms.example: A pill shape behind the icon of the current tab.

terms.plain: How the parts are sorted from smallest to biggest, and what each one is called.
terms.designer: The five levels: tokens, primitives, components, patterns and templates, with Brad Frost's atomic names kept as aliases. An alias table resolves collisions, such as Tag meaning chip in Carbon.
terms.engineer: Not a token; the chosen level and component names would become token path segments such as comp.button (proposed). Each catalog entry's Names line feeds the cross-system alias table.
terms.example: A Tag in one system is called a Chip in another.

terms.plain: Common ways to join parts to do a job, like a sign-up form, plus whole pages.
terms.designer: Recurring solutions that combine components around a user goal: forms, feedback, navigation, disclosure, empty states, plus page templates and layout archetypes. Most UX behavior rules apply here.
terms.engineer: No DTCG type exists for patterns; they compose components and reference tokens. Behavior-rule lint, such as a dialog with no dismiss path, is planned (spec 6.4, 7.12), not built.
terms.example: A sign-up form: fields, labels, a button and error messages together.

terms.plain: Rules for AI tools: say what AI made, show where facts come from, and let people fix it.
terms.designer: Label AI content, place distinctly styled citations next to claims, express uncertainty, and pair every generated result with Edit, Undo and Retry. Never autoscroll streamed answers.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: color.ai.* (proposed) or an AI accent role, and an icon.ai (proposed) glyph; streaming reuses motion tokens. Announce streamed text at completion or in chunks.
terms.designer_says: AI labels, citations, edit and retry
terms.example: A chat answer with numbered sources and a Retry button.

terms.plain: How a long list is split up: page numbers, a Load more button, or scrolling that never ends.
terms.designer: Pagination for tables and goal-directed search, Load more for result lists, infinite scroll only for feeds. Infinite scroll hides the footer and makes items hard to find again.
terms.engineer: No new tokens; pagination reuses button and link tokens. Infinite scroll harms keyboard and footer access, so accessible feeds follow the APG Feed pattern.
terms.example: Search results with page numbers; a social feed that keeps scrolling.

terms.plain: If a delete can be taken back with Undo, or if the app asks you first.
terms.designer: Reversible actions get undo and no confirmation; irreversible or costly ones get a dialog with verb labels like Delete file, and Cancel as the safe default. Overused confirmations breed habituation.
terms.engineer: APG Alert Dialog (role alertdialog), focus returned to the invoker. Undo toast timing is a DTCG duration and must be pausable. Planned warning: delete with neither undo nor confirm.
terms.example: Deleting an email shows Undo; deleting an account asks first.

terms.plain: Keeping extra choices out of sight until you need them, so the screen stays clean.
terms.designer: Show key options first and put advanced ones behind a labeled trigger, like More options. Use at most two levels, and never hide anything essential behind hover.
terms.engineer: Triggers expose expanded or collapsed state through APG Accordion or Disclosure (aria-expanded, aria-controls). Components: accordion, toggletip, popover, sheet, tabs, steps for staged disclosure. No token; it is a pattern rule.
terms.example: An Advanced settings link that opens more choices.

terms.plain: What a screen shows when there is nothing in it yet, and what you can do next.
terms.designer: Cover first use, user-cleared and no-results cases. Each communicates status, teaches the feature, and offers a direct next step with a call to action. Loading is not an empty state.
terms.engineer: Reuses spacing and type tokens plus illustration assets. Status must be real text, not only an image. Lint for a missing empty variant: proposed, not built. Example: Primer Blankslate.
terms.designer_says: empty states: first use, no results
terms.example: No projects yet, with a Create project button.

terms.plain: How an app tells you it is busy, that it worked, or that it went wrong.
terms.designer: How the system reports waiting, results and errors: the loading ladder, the choice of message channel, and the error message pattern. They implement the heuristic of visible status and feedback.
terms.engineer: Composes alerts, toasts, progress bars, spinners, skeletons and empty states. Announce changes through live regions (WCAG 4.1.3) without stealing focus. Duration threshold tokens are not generated yet.
terms.example: A spinner while saving, then a Saved message.

terms.plain: Telling people what went wrong and how to fix it, in plain words, right next to the problem.
terms.designer: Follow NN/g's 13 guidelines: shown near the source, visible without relying on color, precise, constructive and blame-free, input kept. Template: what happened, then how to fix it.
terms.engineer: Tokens: color.text.danger, color.bg.danger.subtle, color.border.danger; a status icon glyph is not generated. Message template {problem}{cause?}{remedy}. Planned lint: color-only error state (spec 6.4).
terms.designer_says: what happened, then how to fix
terms.example: That email is already in use. Sign in instead?

terms.plain: What the app shows while you wait: nothing for a blink, a filling bar for a long wait.
terms.designer: Acknowledge within 50 ms, show nothing under about 1 s, use a skeleton for 1 to 10 s page loads, and past 10 s show determinate progress with cancel.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: DTCG duration tokens feedback.acknowledge.max (proposed) = 50ms and feedback.indicator.delay (proposed) = 1000ms. Pair aria-busy with a polite live region; indicators carry text labels.
terms.example: A page shows gray outlines of its content while it loads.

terms.plain: Choosing where a message shows up: beside the cause, in a bar up top, or in a quick pop-up.
terms.designer: Put the message where the cause is, inline or in a banner by default. Toasts only for low-stakes confirmations with undo; Primer ships none. Dialogs only for blocking decisions.
terms.engineer: Four status roles, such as color.bg.danger.subtle and color.text.danger. Use live regions (WCAG 4.1.3) without moving focus; never auto-dismiss a toast holding an action.
terms.example: A Deleted, Undo toast after removing an email.

terms.plain: How a form is set up: a name above each box, a tip, and a star on must-fill boxes.
terms.designer: A visible label above every field, a hint below it, an asterisk at the label start with a legend, and autofill on standard inputs. Placeholder-only labels are a planned warning.
terms.engineer: Set autocomplete on personal-data inputs and expose required state to assistive tech, not only an asterisk. Unlabeled fields are a planned lint error. Label gap: a space.stack.* step.
terms.example: Email, with a star and the hint We never share it.

terms.plain: When a form checks your answers and where it shows mistakes: by each box, at the top, or both.
terms.designer: Sources disagree: one validates on submit, the other on blur. Both reject flagging errors mid-typing. Forms over about 5 fields show an error summary plus inline messages.
terms.engineer: A prop validateOn: blur | submit | change, with revalidateOn: change. Errors identified in text and linked to fields (WCAG 3.3.1); focus the summary on submit. GOV.UK sets novalidate.
terms.example: A phone number is checked when you leave the box, not while typing.

terms.plain: Tiny views you read in a blink without opening the app, like a watch face.
terms.designer: Widgets, complications, tiles, notifications and Live Activities. Design the complication or tile first, then the app, with one number or one status per surface. Always On dims them.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: numeral type styles such as type.numeral.lg (proposed), compact spacing and an ambient mode that dims secondary content. Content descriptions must match exactly what is shown.
terms.example: A watch face showing the next meeting time.

terms.plain: Screen shapes many apps share, like a list on the left and details on the right.
terms.designer: Named screen structures that recur across products: canonical pane layouts such as list-detail, supporting pane and feed, and the app shell that holds navigation, header and content.
terms.engineer: Compose ships canonical layout scaffolds; SwiftUI has NavigationSplitView and UIKit UISplitViewController. Pane and rail width tokens are not generated yet. Landmarks follow pane order.
terms.example: An email app: folder list, message list and open message.

terms.plain: Ways to split a screen into one, two or three parts side by side, based on how wide it is.
terms.designer: Material's list-detail, supporting pane and feed layouts. One pane below 840dp, two from 840dp, three only at 1600dp and up, with the supporting pane about a third.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: layout.pane.fixed.expanded (proposed) = 360 (dp; exported as px), layout.pane.fixed.large (proposed) = 412, layout.pane.supporting.ratio (proposed) = 0.333, a DTCG number.
terms.example: On a tablet, the inbox list and the open email side by side.

terms.plain: The parts of an app that stay put, like the menu and top bar, while the main content changes.
terms.designer: The persistent regions: navigation, header, content and supporting areas. Compact screens use a bottom bar with 3 to 5 destinations, medium a collapsed rail, expanded a rail or sidebar.
terms.engineer: Not generated yet: layout.rail.width.collapsed (proposed), layout.sidebar.width (proposed), layout.header.height (proposed), DTCG dimensions. Swap only functionally equivalent components. Examples: Carbon UI shell, SwiftUI NavigationSplitView.
terms.example: A sidebar and header that stay while pages change in the middle.

terms.plain: How the screen moves as you go to the next one, and the order things show up in.
terms.designer: Fade, fade through, shared axis and container transform, which visibly links an element to what it opens. Stagger items 20 to 50 ms apart, at most 500 ms total.
terms.engineer: Transitions are named by role as DTCG transition composites: motion.transition.feedback, enter, exit, move, expand. No named patterns or stagger tokens exist; reduced motion swaps movement for a fade.
terms.designer_says: container transform, shared axis, fade through
terms.example: A card grows into the detail page when you tap it.

terms.plain: How an app's main menu works: how many places, how deep it goes, and if it stays in view.
terms.designer: Keep primary navigation visible whenever width allows. Do not cap items at seven, a misuse of Miller's law; group long lists and test labels with a tree test.
terms.engineer: A pattern setting rather than a token, such as nav.visibleItems.compact (proposed) = 5, not generated yet. Expose the nav landmark and aria-current; keep placement consistent (WCAG 3.2.3).
terms.example: Five tabs that stay visible at the bottom of a phone app.

terms.term: Navigation containers by size, platform and device
terms.plain: The same places to go, shown as a bottom bar on phones and a side list on laptops.
terms.designer: 3 to 5 destinations: bottom bar on phone, rail on tablet, sidebar on desktop; more than 7 go in a grouped sidebar. Keep destinations identical and swap only the container.
terms.engineer: A rule table from context and breakpoint to container; tokens like nav.bar.height (proposed) and nav.rail.width.collapsed (proposed) are not generated yet. Natives: SwiftUI sidebarAdaptable, Compose NavigationRail.
terms.example: Tabs on the phone become a sidebar on the iPad.

terms.plain: How new people learn an app: tips when they need them, not a tour they must sit through.
terms.designer: No forced tour. Use contextual help and empty states that teach, and make everything skippable. Deck-of-cards tutorials make the interface look more complicated than it is.
terms.engineer: No tokens. Coachmarks reuse Tooltip or Popover and need dialog-style focus management, keyboard access and a dismiss control. Lint for a tour with no skip control: proposed, not built.
terms.example: A tip that appears the first time you open the editor.

terms.plain: More jobs apps often need, like search, filters, signing in, big tables and settings.
terms.designer: Search and filtering, authentication, data tables and settings, catalogued without their own Decision Card. Their choices come from the components involved and the forms, collections and feedback patterns.
terms.engineer: Examples: filters compose Search field, Combobox, Chips and Sheet; sign-in allows paste and password managers (WCAG 3.3.8); interactive tables use APG Grid, static ones Table.
terms.example: A sign-in screen that lets a password manager fill the password.

terms.plain: Which pop-up to use: a center box, a panel that slides in, or a small box next to a button.
terms.designer: Dialog for short decisions, side sheet for editing with context, bottom sheet on phones, popover for small scoped tasks. Follow each platform's button order, and always give a way out.
terms.engineer: APG Dialog (Modal): focus trapped and returned, Escape closes, aria-modal. iOS sheets use detents and a grabber (UISheetPresentationController). A dialog with no dismiss path is a planned lint error.
terms.example: A bottom sheet with share options on a phone.

terms.plain: Whole pages to start from, like a dashboard, a list page, a detail page or a settings page.
terms.designer: Whole-page starting points assembled from shell, components and patterns: dashboard, list or index, detail, settings, and marketing or landing page. Detail pages use a supporting pane of about one third.
terms.engineer: Product systems ship the shell as components: Primer PageLayout, Carbon UI shell and Polaris Page; marketing templates mostly live outside them. A reference site's page structure can be extracted.
terms.example: A dashboard with a sidebar, a header and a grid of cards.

terms.plain: The checks that keep work made by people and AI inside the rules.
terms.designer: The checks that keep human and agent work inside the rules: which rules run, where (editor, export, CI), how strict they are, and which device safety and accessibility tests apply.
terms.engineer: The enforcement layer for prin.ux.rules, visual principles and foundation constraints. Today engine.py validate checks tokens and engine.py review scans code; exported lint configs are planned.

terms.plain: The full list of tests the tool runs, like checking text is easy to read on its background.
terms.designer: What engine.py validate checks: contrast pairs in every mode, target sizes, focus, reduced motion, hierarchy counts and Figma mode limits. Label, dismiss and deceptive-pattern checks are planned.
terms.engineer: validate resolves every alias without cycles, requires a $type, keeps modifiers orthogonal and warns past the Figma plan's mode cap. The Figma export warns above 5,000 variables.
terms.designer_says: contrast, target, label and limit checks
terms.code_name: engine.py validate: contrast, targets, aliases, limits

terms.plain: How tough the tool is when it reviews your look: a gentle coach, a strict gate, or a score sheet.
terms.designer: How strongly the builder critiques visual choices: coaching by default; strict blocking and a metrics panel are planned. Every validate message names its rule, so users learn the vocabulary.
terms.engineer: Not tokens. Q-pref-01 (silent, coach, strict or metrics) is planned, so the interview skips it. validate reports errors, build stops on them, and review --strict fails on hard-coded values.

terms.plain: How rules hold: you can only break one on purpose, and AI helpers must obey the same rules.
terms.designer: Rules bind people and agents alike: raw values only through an explicit detach, agents limited to the same scopes as humans, and lint rules planned for every generated system.
terms.engineer: Planned: a lint/ folder with a stylelint strict-value config (spec 7.12). Today engine.py review flags hard-coded values and validate checks contrast; Figma export scopes semantic variables.
terms.designer_says: same rules for people and agents

terms.plain: Hard rules for places where a screen could put people at risk, like while they drive a car.
terms.designer: Hard rules where a design can endanger people, such as driving or headsets. In a vehicle context they should be errors, not warnings; OpenDesigner enforces 76 px targets today.
terms.engineer: With car in raw.platforms or vehicle in raw.inputs, validate enforces a 76 px target. vehicle.animation (proposed) is planned; driving limits: 2 s glance, 12 s task.

terms.plain: The smallest set of tests with helper tools, like screen readers, done on each kind of device.
terms.designer: The minimum assistive-technology tests per shipped device class: one screen reader, one motor alternative and the largest text size. A first-class device means first-class assistive tech.
terms.engineer: Not tokens. DESIGN.md's Accessibility section lists the test matrix: keyboard, a screen reader per platform, 200% zoom, forced colors and reduced motion. Per-component checklists are planned.

terms.plain: How the finished design leaves the tool and stays in step with design apps and code.
terms.designer: How the system leaves the builder and stays in sync: source of truth, interchange file, build pipeline, packaging, export channels, agent-readable outputs, and the round trip with design tools.
terms.engineer: Parent of the deliver.* nodes. engine.py generate turns state.json into DTCG 2025.10 plus a resolver; export turns that into CSS, Tailwind, Swift, Compose, Figma, Paper and DTCG.
terms.code_name: DTCG plus resolver, then platform code

terms.plain: The files and links that let AI helpers read your design and follow it.
terms.designer: How AI agents read the system: MCP servers, llms.txt, DESIGN.md and Markdown twins of docs. Ship one live channel and one file channel, and test with evals.
terms.engineer: Today: DTCG files with $description text, DESIGN.md with a For Agents section, and an AGENTS.md snippet. An MCP server is planned (spec Phase 2).

terms.plain: The ways to send your design out of the tool, like copying code or sending it to a design app.
terms.designer: How a system leaves the tool. OpenDesigner writes export files and pushes to Figma or Paper through their MCP; a CLI URL and pull requests are not built.
terms.engineer: Today: DTCG (canonical), CSS custom properties, Tailwind v4 @theme, Swift, Compose, and Figma and Paper payloads. An MCP server is planned (spec Phase 2).
terms.designer_says: exports: CSS, DTCG, native code, Figma

terms.plain: The shared file type that tools use to pass your choices back and forth, and how it is split.
terms.designer: The standard file format tokens travel in, and how the files split. Default: DTCG 2025.10, one file per tier and mode, which maps directly onto Figma's one-file-per-mode import.
terms.engineer: One file per tier and mode (semantic.color.dark.tokens.json), plus opendesigner.resolver.json with sets and modifiers. DTCG 2025.10 is stable but not a W3C Standard.

terms.plain: How the tool sends your design to drawing apps like Figma and gets changes back.
terms.designer: How the builder mirrors the system into design tools and captures changes back. No tool found does deterministic two-way token sync, so Figma and Paper are treated as mirrors.
terms.engineer: Figma: the remote MCP use_figma with a Full seat, else build/figma/import, one DTCG file per collection and mode. Paper: its local MCP. Penpot: imports the DTCG files.
terms.code_name: use_figma MCP or DTCG per mode

terms.plain: How your design shows up in Figma, an app where many people draw screens.
terms.designer: How tokens and components appear in Figma: variable collections and modes, scopes and publishing, code syntax, styles versus variables, and Code Connect links to code.
terms.engineer: Figma imports color (sRGB, HSL), dimension (px), fontFamily, duration (s), number and a non-standard string. DTCG composites become styles, not variables.

terms.plain: Links from each drawn part in Figma to the real code part, with notes that help AI helpers.
terms.designer: Links from Figma components to real code components, plus descriptions and examples Figma's AI tools read. Start with the top 20 components; describe every component and semantic variable.
terms.engineer: Code Connect needs an Organization or Enterprise plan. Descriptions go in $description; get_variable_defs returns variable names and values. The remote MCP needs a frame or layer link.

terms.plain: The code name Figma shows next to each value, so designers and coders call it the same thing.
terms.designer: The code name Figma's Dev Mode shows beside each variable for Web, Android and iOS. It is the join key between canvas and code, so both sides use one name.
terms.engineer: REST codeSyntax {WEB, ANDROID, iOS}, from the CSS export's name transform: color/surface/base becomes var(--ds-color-surface-base), DS.Colors.surfaceBase on iOS. No Flutter or React Native slot.

terms.plain: Which choices Figma keeps as one setting and which as a bundle, like a text style.
terms.designer: Which values live as Figma variables and which as styles. Rule: variables for values, styles for bundles; any single value that changes by mode must be a variable.
terms.engineer: Colors, spacing, radius, sizes, opacity and motion become variables. OpenDesigner writes text styles bound to size, weight and family variables, and effect styles for elevation; no gradients or grids.
terms.designer_says: variables for values, styles for bundles
terms.code_name: text and effect styles, not variables

terms.plain: How Figma groups your saved choices, and hides the raw ones so no one picks them by mistake.
terms.designer: How tiers map to Figma collections and modes. Hide all primitives and scope each semantic variable to the properties its name says, so designers only see the right choices.
terms.engineer: Collections: Primitives (hidden), Color (Light, Dark), Density (Spacious, Comfortable, Compact), Motion (Standard, Reduced), Tokens. REST scopes such as TEXT_FILL; hiddenFromPublishing: true; 5,000 variables per collection.

terms.plain: Paper is a design app made of web pages; it takes your colors, but light and dark need two sets.
terms.designer: An HTML and CSS design canvas that agents can write to. Its tokens have no modes or libraries, so use it for specimens, not as the source of truth.
terms.engineer: A local MCP server with 34 tools, including write_html and create_tokens. Tokens are CSS variables with no modes or DTCG, so light and dark need separate sets.

terms.plain: Penpot is a free, open design app that can load and save the shared design file.
terms.designer: Penpot is an open-source design tool with multi-dimensional themes. It is the only tool the research found that imports and exports DTCG tokens natively.
terms.engineer: Native DTCG import and export, using $themes.json and $metadata.json alongside the token sets, with multi-dimensional themes.

terms.plain: How coders get the kit into their app, like adding a package or pasting in the code.
terms.designer: How engineers consume the system: an npm library, copy-in source like shadcn, a CDN runtime, CSS and HTML only, headless primitives, or utilities like Tailwind.
terms.engineer: Generate DTCG JSON first, then emit CSS variables and a Tailwind @theme, which OpenDesigner does today. Web components work across frameworks.

terms.plain: A tool that turns one design file into code that web and phone apps can use right away.
terms.designer: The build tool that turns one token source into platform code. Default: Terrazzo for web-only teams, Style Dictionary v5 when native iOS or Android outputs are needed.
terms.engineer: Consumes DTCG 2025.10 plus resolver: Terrazzo 2.x supports resolvers; Style Dictionary v5 needs each mode pre-expanded. engine.py export writes CSS, Swift and Compose; pipeline configs are planned.

terms.term: Durable records for later sessions and the team
terms.plain: Files saved in your project, so the next chat or your team knows what you chose and why.
terms.designer: DESIGN.md is the readable spec, a decision log keeps every choice with its reason, and RATIONALE.md explains it to your team. Later sessions build on them without drift.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/tokens/ (DTCG, canonical), state.json and decisions.md, plus DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md at the root. engine.py design-md refreshes them; engine.py review finds drift.

terms.term: Source of truth and round-trip direction
terms.plain: The one main copy that all other copies follow, and which way changes flow.
terms.designer: Which copy wins and how changes flow. In OpenDesigner, state.json and the DTCG files it generates are canonical; Figma and Paper are mirrors whose edits return as recorded decisions.
terms.engineer: engine.py build compiles state.json to DTCG 2025.10 plus resolver and code; Figma variables carry matching code syntax. JSON-first keeps OKLCH and P3 values Figma import drops.

terms.plain: How the kit is run over time: who looks after it, how it grows, and how it changes.
terms.designer: How the system runs as a product over time: build order and pilots, team, contribution, decisions, status labels, versioning, deprecation, documentation, rollout and measurement.
terms.engineer: Parent of the gov.* nodes. No tokens: team notes in context.team, the decision log in decisions.md, the component list in components.inventory; status and versioning fields are proposed.

terms.plain: How the kit is brought to product teams, step by step, and how they are kept up to date.
terms.designer: How the system reaches product teams and keeps them informed. Default: incremental rollout led by pain points, plus release notes, a public roadmap and a support channel.
terms.engineer: opendesigner-extend ends each change with a change note: what, why, affects, validation, decision id. Release notes from token diffs and a migration checklist are not built. Native apps migrate slower.
terms.code_name: extend change note; release notes (not built)

terms.plain: How each new release is numbered and when releases come out.
terms.designer: How releases are numbered and scheduled. Default: one semantic version for the whole library while small, per-package versions once there is more than one platform, on a predictable cadence.
terms.engineer: No release version is stored yet. package.version (proposed) per artifact: tokens, components-web, components-ios, figma-library. Native ships via SPM or Gradle while Figma publishes separately, so aligning versions needs automation.

terms.plain: How old parts are phased out with warning, and how teams get help moving to new ones.
terms.designer: Deprecate in a minor release, remove in the next major, give at least one release cycle of notice, and pair every removal with a codemod or migration guide.
terms.engineer: DTCG $deprecated (boolean or string, "Use color.bg.accent (v4)") plus $description, not emitted yet; component.deprecated {since, removeIn, replacement} is proposed. Figma variables have no deprecated flag.

terms.plain: How people outside the core team can suggest or add new parts to the kit.
terms.designer: How outsiders add to the system. Default: a fast lane for fixes, icons and docs, and a proposal lane for new components, gated by useful and unique.
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-gov-03 (two-lanes by default); governance.contribution {who, types, criteria} is proposed. Proposals must pass the useful-and-unique gate before any build work starts.

terms.plain: The steps a change goes through, and how each choice and its reason are written down.
terms.designer: The steps a change goes through and how decisions are recorded. Adopt Brad Frost's 10-step flow and log every foundation decision as an architecture decision record, as OpenDesigner does.
terms.engineer: opendesigner/decisions.md is append-only and ADR-style: each D-0001 entry records path = value, set_by, locked, date, supersedes, source_ref and reason. RFC records and status fields are proposed.

terms.plain: Where the how-to guides for the kit live, and who is allowed to write them.
terms.designer: Where documentation lives and who writes it. Small teams document in Figma plus Storybook, add a docs platform when non-engineers author, and always publish a machine-readable export.
terms.engineer: OpenDesigner generates DESIGN.md from the same data; component pages (spec 7.8) are planned. Storybook's component manifest supports React, Angular (Vite) and Vue 3 (Vite).

terms.plain: The fixed layout of the help page for each part, like when to use it and how.
terms.designer: The template for each component's page: usage, when not to use, anatomy, variants, states, content, accessibility, code and changelog. Docs complete is part of the definition of done.
terms.engineer: Planned (spec 7.8), not generated: opendesigner/components/<name>.md with when to use, when not, anatomy, variants, states, content, accessibility, code and changelog.

terms.plain: Labels that show if a part is still being tried, ready to use, or on its way out.
terms.designer: The states a component can be in. Default three, experimental, ready and deprecated, which is enough for most teams; Primer itself simplified from five to three.
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-gov-04. DESIGN.md shows each component's status from components.notes, default "planned (tokens ready)"; component.status (proposed) = experimental | ready | deprecated.

terms.plain: How you tell if teams use the kit and like it, and how grown-up the kit is.
terms.designer: How adoption and value are measured and which maturity stage you target. Start with design adoption from Figma analytics, code adoption from a scanner, and a quarterly satisfaction survey.
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-gov-05; metrics[] {name, source, target} (proposed) and system.maturityStage (proposed), 1-4 after Sparkbox's four stages, are not stored. Native code usage needs its own scanners.

terms.plain: The order you build things in, and which real app tries the kit first.
terms.designer: The build order and which product pilots the system. Default: minimal foundations (color roles, type, spacing, radius), then components the pilot needs, then back-fill foundations as gaps appear.
terms.engineer: No tokens. Recorded as answers.Q-gov-02; pilots[] {product, score, champion, window} is proposed. Score 2-3 candidates on Dan Mall's 8 criteria and pick one with a champion.

terms.plain: Who looks after the kit, one central team or people spread across teams, and what jobs they do.
terms.designer: Who owns the system (centralized, federated or hybrid) and which roles staff it. Default: start centralized with a named owner, even at 1-2 people; add federated contributors later.
terms.engineer: Recorded as answers.Q-scope-04 (size and model) and context.team, printed in PRODUCT.md; team.roles[] is proposed. Native platforms need iOS and Android engineers.

terms.plain: Tools in Figma that keep things tidy: a checker, counts of what is used, and side copies for trying changes.
terms.designer: Figma's built-in governance: the Check designs linter, library analytics and branching. On Organization or Enterprise, run Check designs before Ready for dev and review analytics quarterly.
terms.engineer: Check designs lints one page at a time, caps at 25K layers and ranks partly by variable naming. OpenDesigner's validate and review lint tokens and code; no analytics.

terms.plain: Choices about the tool you use to make the kit, not about the kit itself.
terms.designer: Decisions about the OpenDesigner tool rather than the system it makes: how you edit, preview, explore, review and collaborate. Today that is a chat interview with visual templates.
terms.engineer: A meta layer for decisions about the tool. Today OpenDesigner is skills, an engine script and HTML templates in the host; a standalone canvas is optional phase 3.

terms.plain: How the AI helper suggests changes you can check first, and how it shows you other options.
terms.designer: Planned: agent edits as reviewable before-and-after patches, and shuffle. Today the agent shows old and new values before a change, locks protect decisions, and option-gallery compares directions.
terms.engineer: Planned: patches {op, path, from, to, rationale} and variants {seed, locked[], params}. Today each change is engine.py set with --why, logged in decisions.md; locks sit in state.json.
terms.designer_says: reviewable agent patches, lock and shuffle
terms.example: Lock the brand color so later changes cannot move it.

terms.plain: What the work area shows: real, working web parts, a flat picture, or a scene from a design app.
terms.designer: What the canvas renders: real HTML and CSS components, a flat image, or a design-tool scene graph. Default: real HTML and CSS, ideally the actual component library.
terms.engineer: preview.html is real HTML and CSS: tokens are CSS custom properties and modes are [data-theme] selectors or @media blocks. SwiftUI and Compose outputs get no preview yet.
terms.code_name: CSS custom properties, modes as selectors

terms.plain: Whether a few people and AI helpers can work on one design at once, and how you see them.
terms.designer: Whether people and agents edit together, and how presence shows. Version 1 is single-user and local-first; agent presence is planned first, since agents are the most frequent co-editors.
terms.engineer: Version 1 keeps state in files in your repo (state.json, decisions.md), so git gives history. Planned: edits as operations (CRDT or operational transform), which also give undo.

terms.plain: The knobs and sliders you use to set the basics, like picking one starting color.
terms.designer: The widgets that edit foundations. OpenDesigner is generator-first: seed color and contrast target, base size and ratio, space unit; raw values only through an explicit detach.
terms.engineer: Dials and raw inputs in state.json are the source; tokens are derived, with provenance in $extensions.opendesigner.source (formula or person). OKLCH values carry hex fallbacks for Figma.

terms.plain: How you add OpenDesigner to the AI app you already use.
terms.designer: You load OpenDesigner into your own AI: a Claude plugin, a skills folder that Codex, Cursor and Copilot find, or a ChatGPT Project with five files.
terms.engineer: skills/ is the source; sync_skills.py copies it to .agents/skills and .claude/skills. Manifests: .claude-plugin/ and plugin.json. build_dist.py makes the zip. A server is planned.
terms.designer_says: install as a skill or plugin

terms.plain: If the tool cannot make something well, like a logo, it asks whether you have one or can get one.
terms.designer: For what AI cannot make well, like logos, custom icons, illustration, photography or a brand typeface, the builder asks for yours, or suggests a designer or a named tool.
terms.engineer: state.json hooks.H-logo and 13 others store {status, files, note}; status is pending, have, commissioning, tool, open-library, placeholder or not-needed. DESIGN.md lists open ones under Open Items.

terms.plain: Being able to do every task in the tool with the keyboard, no mouse needed.
terms.designer: Planned for a canvas: a Cmd+K palette, single keys for toggles like light and dark, arrow-key nudging with Shift for big steps. Today everything runs by typing in chat.
terms.engineer: Planned: a palette indexing every action and token path; Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere; arrows nudge perceptual values. Today OD: lines and engine commands are the keyboard path.

terms.plain: Adding a sample site or picture so the AI can learn from how it is made, without copying its brand.
terms.designer: Add a website, screenshot or Figma file at any time; the AI reads its color, type, spacing, radius, motion and components, and builds on its structure, never another brand's identity.
terms.engineer: css_scan.py or Figma's get_variable_defs and get_design_context measure values; engine.py intake fits them to dials with confidence levels, pending in state.json references.

terms.plain: Your main way of working in the tool: sliders with a live view, a drawing space, a chat, or code.
terms.designer: Research default: panels with live preview, a canvas for screens, and the agent as an accelerator, never the only path. Today OpenDesigner is agent-led: chat, visual templates and OD: lines.
terms.engineer: Each control binds to one path: a dial or raw input that derives many tokens (raw.brandColor), a question id, or a token path. Templates return OD:set lines.
terms.designer_says: interaction model: chat, panels or canvas

terms.plain: Big choices get more time and pictures to compare. Small ones get a quick yes.
terms.designer: The interview slows down where a choice shapes the most: one big decision per turn, with visual options. Small ones come grouped with a default you confirm.
terms.engineer: pacing.json sets zoom levels 0-3 and each question's time weight (high at fan-out 5+). Questions offer 2 to 4 options, one recommended; owner inputs are never invented.

terms.plain: What you see as you decide, like light and dark sample screens side by side, and how fast it updates.
terms.designer: What you see while deciding: specimens for each scale, a component sheet and every mode side by side (engine.py preview). Live re-rendering while you drag a control is planned.
terms.engineer: preview.html binds components to semantic CSS variables, so each [data-theme] block shows a mode without code changes. The page is static; progress indicators for slow updates are planned.
terms.designer_says: live specimens, all modes side by side

terms.plain: How changes get checked before they go out: the page before, the problems marked on it, then the page after.
terms.designer: review.py compare shows the page today, the audit drawn on it and the fix, each with what it improves. Planned: a diff per change set, in every mode.
terms.engineer: review.py compare builds one HTML file from two screenshots and __od.marks() boxes. Planned: walk the alias graph to find the components a token change moves.

terms.plain: How the tool keeps your steps and saves versions, and whether you can undo or share work by a link.
terms.designer: How the tool keeps history and shares work. Today: state.json and an append-only decisions.md in your repo; git gives versions and branches. Undo and state URLs are planned.
terms.engineer: state.json (schema_version 1) holds the inputs; decisions.md logs every change, and a later entry supersedes an earlier one. A compact URL encoding and coalesced undo are planned.

terms.plain: Where you see your choices as pictures, and how your pick gets back to the AI.
terms.designer: Options show up in the richest visual your AI app allows, from an artifact or a local page down to plain text. Your pick comes back as a short line.
terms.engineer: Eight JSON-fed templates in assets/templates render through show.py or an artifact. Copy my choice emits OD: lines the engine runs. An MCP App view is planned.
